article_content: On October 4, 2011, 10-month-old Lisa Irwin disappeared from her crib in her Kansas City home while her mother and two brothers slept. Her parents believe an intruder entered through a tampered front window. Johnny Tanko, a local handyman known as 'Jersey', was seen in the neighborhood that night and is currently being questioned by police — though he is not considered a suspect. Police found a backpack and used diapers in an abandoned house near the Irwin home, along with soiled diapers in nearby woods. Authorities say these items appear to have been there for some time and are not necessarily linked to the case. In response to the ongoing search, Missouri Governor Jay Nixon deployed 25 members of the National Guard’s Military Police Company to assist local investigators. A $100,000 reward has been offered by anonymous donors for information leading to Lisa’s safe return or the conviction of anyone involved in her disappearance. Lisa’s cousin, Mike Lerette, made an emotional public appeal, saying he would 'gladly give my life to bring Lisa home safely.' Private investigator Bill Stanton, known as 'Wild Bill,' has been hired by an anonymous wealthy family to support the search. He has no access to official police files and is limited to reviewing publicly available information. Over 500 tips have been investigated, including reports of a couple seen near Lisa’s age. More than 30 detectives are assigned to the case, which has drawn national attention after nearly two weeks with no suspects or clear leads. Hours before Lisa was last seen, her uncle was recorded purchasing alcohol and baby wipes — a detail revealed this week to clarify his presence near the home.

article_content: Holidaymakers who splurge on the new Apple Watch won’t have to worry about being locked out of their hotel room. At least one major hotel chain is developing an app to prevent this issue. When the Apple Watch launches in 2015, Starwood Hotels’ app will let guests unlock their room doors without fumbling for a key or digging through bags for a key card. The feature was unveiled during Apple’s product event earlier this week, where an image of Starwood’s app was displayed. With the Apple Watch acting as a digital room key, guests with a compatible iPhone simply need to tap a button while standing at the door. The app will be available at select Starwood Hotels and Resorts Worldwide properties—including Westin, Sheraton, W, and Aloft—starting next spring. The Apple Watch will not come cheap: prices start at $349 (approximately £215) in the US, though UK pricing has not yet been announced. Starwood recently made headlines for introducing a robot butler named Botlr at its Aloft hotel in Silicon Valley. The autonomous device delivers amenities from the front desk to any of the hotel’s 150 rooms in under three minutes. Apps that unlock hotel doors represent the future of hospitality, as travel companies strive to enhance guest convenience. Hilton Hotels has also announced plans to replace traditional keys with smartphones, while American Airlines is partnering with Apple to develop an Apple Watch app for managing flight bookings.

article_content: A 24-year-old Romanian woman was fatally stabbed on a busy road in Ilford, Essex, and collapsed at a local fast-food shop, Pizza and Chicken 4 U, shortly after midnight on October 29, 2013. Paramedics administered first aid at the scene, and she was rushed to the Royal London Hospital, where she later died at 1:53am. A 48-year-old man was arrested later that day in connection with the killing and remains in custody at a police station in East London. Police have cordoned off the surrounding streets as investigations continue, and officers from Scotland Yard’s Homicide and Major Crime Command are assisting local units. Witnesses described the scene as chaotic, with multiple police vehicles and sirens filling the area. One neighbor recalled seeing only the victim’s feet inside the shop before staff pulled down the shutters. The victim’s identity has been confirmed by authorities but will not be publicly disclosed until her next of kin have been notified. A post-mortem examination was conducted to determine the precise cause of death. Some local residents mentioned long-standing concerns about prostitution in the neighborhood, though police have not linked the crime to this issue.

article_content: Tottenham’s interest in Victor Wanyama is reinforced by statistics from his defensive midfield performances at Southampton. Mauricio Pochettino is considering signing the Kenyan midfielder over the summer after utilizing him as a defensive shield during his time at St Mary’s. Tottenham recorded the ninth-best defensive record in the Premier League last season, and the new manager believes this must improve if they are to compete for Champions League qualification. When Wanyama was on the pitch, Southampton averaged 1.58 points per game and conceded a goal every 121 minutes. Without him, those figures dropped to 1.28 points per game and one goal every 57 minutes. Though not always among Southampton’s most celebrated players, the 22-year-old was regarded by Pochettino as the team’s unsung hero. Wanyama joined Southampton from Celtic for £12 million last summer, earning praise from opposition managers for his performances against Liverpool, Chelsea, and Arsenal—until a chipped bone sidelined him in January. Pochettino brought him back early, but Wanyama only regained full fitness toward the end of the season. Tottenham are also monitoring Jay Rodriguez, though no formal bid has been made for Adam Lallana, who is widely expected to join Liverpool.

article_content: A 17-year-old teenager, Alyssa Barrett, has been formally charged with murder and burglary following the death of her mother, DeCarol Deloney-Cain, a 54-year-old United Airlines flight attendant. The victim’s body was discovered bound, wrapped in plastic bags, and hidden inside the trunk of her own car on a quiet dirt road in Gary, Indiana. Police say they traced the crime to Alyssa’s 18-year-old boyfriend, Damarius Wren, who was arrested after a GPS device found in the family home led investigators to the location where the body was abandoned. Deloney-Cain, who frequently traveled internationally, was not reported missing until she failed to show up for work a week after her last flight. Her identity was confirmed using the serial number from her breast implants. Inside the home, authorities found bloodstains, red duct tape matching that used to bind the victim’s limbs, and a bloody wrench in the basement — items reportedly pointed out by Alyssa herself. According to court documents, Alyssa told police that Wren attacked her mother upon her return home on July 3, placing a pillowcase over her head, striking her against the stairs, and stabbing her with a kitchen knife. She claims she hid upstairs and later watched as two of Wren’s friends arrived, helped load the body into plastic bags, and transported it in a car. Alyssa says she followed the vehicle in another car and witnessed the body being left on the roadside. Under threat of a gun, she alleges she was forced to withdraw money from her mother’s bank account. Despite these actions, she has not been charged. Wren, meanwhile, reportedly gave police conflicting stories about how he found the body. He remains in custody without bail, and authorities say additional charges could follow. Deloney-Cain’s brother commended the Gary Police Department for their swift response and thorough investigation.

article_content: Liverpool and Chelsea lock horns at Anfield on Tuesday night in the first leg of their Carling Cup semi-final — renewing one of football’s most intense modern rivalries. Over the past two decades, these two giants have clashed repeatedly in high-stakes cup ties, delivering unforgettable drama across the Champions League, FA Cup, and League Cup. From legendary goals to controversial calls and nail-biting penalties, their encounters have shaped the narrative of English football. In the 2005 Carling Cup Final, Chelsea edged Liverpool 3–2 after extra time. John Arne Riise opened the scoring within seconds, but Steven Gerrard’s own goal leveled things. Didier Drogba and Mateja Kezman then sealed the win for Mourinho’s side — despite being sent off during regulation. Later that year, in the Champions League semi-final, Luis Garcia’s infamous 'ghost goal' — a shot that struck the crossbar and bounced down, sparking debate over whether it crossed the line — gave Liverpool a 1–0 aggregate win. The Reds went on to lift the trophy in Istanbul. The 2005–06 Champions League group stage saw both matches between the clubs end 0–0, highlighting their tactical caution when stakes were lower. In the 2006 FA Cup semi-final, Liverpool triumphed 2–1 at Old Trafford thanks to Riise and Garcia, despite Drogba’s reply. They advanced to beat West Ham in the final. Two years later, in the 2007 UCL semi-final, Liverpool again reached the final after a 1–1 draw and a 4–1 penalty win. Pepe Reina saved crucial spot-kicks from Robben and Geremi, while Dirk Kuyt’s goal sent them to Athens — where they lost 2–1 to AC Milan. Chelsea bounced back in 2008, defeating Liverpool 4–3 on aggregate in the UCL semi-final. Frank Lampard and Drogba struck in extra time after Fernando Torres had equalized. The 2009 quarter-final was a thriller: Chelsea won 7–5 on aggregate after a stunning 4–3 comeback at Stamford Bridge. Drogba, Alex, and Lampard led the charge against a spirited Liverpool side. In 2011, Liverpool turned the tables in the Carling Cup quarter-final, winning 2–0 at Stamford Bridge through Maxi Rodríguez and Martin Kelly — handing a blow to then-Chelsea boss André Villas-Boas. Finally, in the 2012 FA Cup Final, Didier Drogba scored his third FA Cup final goal to help Chelsea defeat Liverpool 2–1. Despite a late rally led by Andy Carroll, Chelsea held firm and went on to win their first Champions League title weeks later. Since 2005, in cup competitions: Chelsea have won six times, Liverpool four, with five draws. Chelsea have scored 19 goals to Liverpool’s 16.

Kwiminyaka ezi-20 ezimene, izinto eziningi zabo ziyabonakala kakhulu kwiindlela ezifanele ngokukhuluma, ziqhubekile kwi-Champions League, FA Cup ne-League Cup. Kwiminyaka e-2011, i-Liverpool zifaka ukuzama kwi-Carling Cup quarter-final, zifaka 2–0 e-Stamford Bridge kusukela ku-Maxi Rodríguez ne-Martin Kelly — zifaka ukubhekisana kwi-André Villas-Boas. article_content: In the quiet mountain town of Aspen, the shocking murder of Nancy Pfister — a vibrant socialite once linked to celebrities like Michael Douglas — has left residents stunned. Found beaten to death in her own home on February 26, just days after returning from Australia, Pfister’s death marks the first homicide in the area since 2001. Three people have now been formally charged: her longtime tenants, William and Nancy Styler, and her trusted property manager, Katherine Carpenter. The Stylers, who had been renting Pfister’s home, were accused of failing to pay rent or utilities — a dispute Pfister publicly lamented on Facebook just weeks before her death. Carpenter, who discovered the body, was arrested shortly afterward despite decades of loyal service to Pfister. Authorities have not ruled out further arrests. Out of caution, Pfister’s surviving family — including her daughter Juliana and two sisters — are under 24-hour security detail. 'They’re not sure if they’ve got them all,' said a source close to the case. The Stylers, once pillars of the community, have a complicated past: William, a former anesthesiologist, struggled financially after losing a major lawsuit and facing serious health issues. Nancy, a renowned horticulturist known worldwide for cultivating giant Victoria water lilies, ran a public garden that welcomed schoolchildren. Neighbors describe them as gentle, even kind — making the charges seem unthinkable. Carpenter, a 20-year veteran at Alpine Bank, was widely liked. One customer said, 'I’d have bet the farm she didn’t do it.' Yet, investigators uncovered her role in managing the property and her presence at the scene. article_content: CNN — The Graha Bhakti Budaya (GBB), a weathered 1960s building and part of Jakarta’s largest arts center, may seem unremarkable from the outside. But on Monday, its theater became a powerful symbol of national reckoning after the Indonesian premiere of the documentary 'The Look of Silence'. 'That screening was a huge moment,' said 54-year-old Irawan Karseno, head of the Jakarta Arts Council. 'Our nation carries deep wounds from 1965. This film is part of a healing process.' Karseno helped bring the film — Joshua Oppenheimer’s companion piece to the Oscar-nominated 'The Act of Killing' — to a captivated audience of about 1,500 people. Oppenheimer’s 2012 film exposed the chilling testimonies of perpetrators in Indonesia’s anti-communist purges of 1965–66, during which human rights groups estimate 500,000 to 1 million people were killed by military death squads, paving the way for General Suharto’s 'New Order' regime. 'The Look of Silence' shifts focus to the survivors. Its central figure is Adi, a 45-year-old optometrist, who seeks to understand why his parents remain traumatized by the 1965 murder of his brother, Ramli — and why fear and denial still dominate his community. Adi’s quiet confrontations with men who admitted to killing his brother stand in stark contrast to the widespread belief among many Indonesians that 'the past is the past.' 'But the younger generation is more open-minded,' Karseno said. 'I was only five when it happened, and I’m still ashamed. Next year marks 50 years since the killings. How do we prepare? Can Indonesia find a path like Germany did after the Holocaust?' In 2012, Indonesia’s National Human Rights Commission officially classified the massacres as gross human rights violations. Yet no one has ever been prosecuted. The Attorney General’s office has not responded to CNN’s requests for comment. Many families of victims still live in fear of retaliation if they speak out. During filming, Oppenheimer took extreme precautions: getaway cars were ready, no one carried ID, phones had no data, and Adi’s family stood by at the airport, prepared to flee at a moment’s notice. 'It’s heartbreaking that Adi and his family had to become fugitives after making this film — all because he sought forgiveness,' Oppenheimer said. 'This shows how far Indonesia still has to go to become a true democracy with rule of law. The perpetrators’ impunity forces victims to run away — while they’ve done something profoundly dignified.' Monday’s premiere was uniquely significant: it was the first public screening of either film organized by Indonesian state institutions — the Jakarta Arts Council and Komnas HAM. Earlier showings of 'The Act of Killing' required heavy security and private venues. This time, the event was openly advertised — a sign that space for dialogue is slowly opening. Community screenings are planned nationwide this December. Encouraged by President Joko Widodo’s election, Karseno remains hopeful. 'We’re pushing hard for Jokowi to watch this film,' he said. 'Our issue isn’t just about the 1960s — it’s about how Indonesia connects with the world.' The atmosphere on Monday was tense with anticipation, not fear. Two screenings were added because demand far exceeded capacity. Adi attended. 'After watching,' Karseno said, 'I felt deep sadness. Then I met Adi — and I cried.'

'Nkqondo eli, kuyakho kakhulu,' uKarseno, osebenzisa ngokukhetha i-Jakarta Arts Council, uze uyithi. 'Sizwe sisebenzisa izinto eziningi ezimnyama e-1965. U-'The Act of Killing' (2012) ubonakala ngokuthi abaninzi baphindele amandla enkosi yamagunya, kanti izinyanga zihamba kakhulu kubalulekile kubantu e-500 000 ku-1 000 000 e-1965–66, ukuze uzalela u-Suharto 'New Order'.  U-'The Look of Silence' ufaka izinto ezintsha kwindlu yabantu abazothando. U-Adi ubonakala ngokukhuluma nabo abadlaliweyo abafika kakhulu kwiindaba ezininzi ezifana ne-'the past is the past'.  'Kodwa abantu abaninzi bayakho kakhulu,' uKarseno. 'Ngingasixhosa ngempela, ngisho, ngenxa yezinto e-1965. Ngokwesikhathi esilungileyo, kuyakho 50 ngelinye. Ngingakufuna ukuthi nini? Ungayithanda ngokuphila nge-Germany kancane?'  Kwiminyaka y-2012, i-National Human Rights Commission iyavumela ukuthi izinto e-1965 ziyizinto ezimbili ezimnyama. Kodwa akukho umntu othandekile. U-Attorney General akawazi ukuthi ukuthi u-CNN. 'Kuyakhala ukuthi u-Adi nezinyanga zakhe zizathunyiwe ngaphambi kwezinto ezimnyama, kodwa ngokuthi uyayithanda ukuthula,' u-Oppenheimer. Kwesikhathi sesithi, kuyakho kakhulu: kuyakho umdlalo wokuziphatha kwindlu yezinto ezimnyama e-Jakarta Arts Council ne-National Human Rights Commission. Kwiminyaka y-2012, kuyakho kakhulu kusengqongqo, kodwa kusengqongqo kwenza izikhathi eziningi.  Kwiminyaka y-December, kuyakho izikhathi eziningi e-Indonesia. U-Karseno, uyavumela ukuthi u-Joko Widodo uyakho, uyayithanda. 'Sizayenza kakhulu ukuthi u-Jokowi uze usebenzise lo mhlaba,' uKarseno. 'Sizwe sisebenzisa izinto e-1960, kodwa sisebenzisa nje ukuthi sithande ngezinyanga zombuso.'  Kwesikhathi sesithi, kuyakho kakhulu kusengqongqo, kodwa akukho ukuthi kuyakho ukuthi kuyakho. article_content: After nearly three weeks of political stalemate, Madhav Kumar Nepal has been unanimously elected Nepal’s new prime minister. The 56-year-old veteran communist, formerly the general secretary of the Communist Party of Nepal (Unified Marxist-Leninist), ran unopposed after securing support from more than 20 of the 25 parties in parliament. His rise comes after Pushpa Kamal Dahal — chair of the former Maoist rebels and previous prime minister — stepped down in early May following a constitutional clash over the dismissal of the army chief. Nepal, who previously served as deputy prime minister in 1995, had temporarily stepped away from leadership after his party underperformed in the 2008 elections, when the Maoists emerged as the largest force with 38% of seats. Since Nepal became a republic in 2008, its government has faced two urgent missions: drafting a new constitution within 12 months and integrating nearly 20,000 former Maoist fighters into the national military and police. Without cooperation from the Maoists — once insurgents who waged a decade-long war to end the monarchy — these goals remain impossible.

article_content: For most of his life, Austin Chapman experienced the world visually. Born profoundly deaf, he could only detect low rumbles through outdated hearing aids—music, voices, and everyday sounds remained out of reach. That changed a month ago when he tried a new pair of bright orange Phonak hearing aids. Suddenly, Mozart’s Lacrimosa flooded his senses, and tears rolled down his cheeks. He wasn’t just hearing music—he was feeling it, for the first time. Songs by Radiohead, Devo, and Pink Floyd unfolded like colors he’d never seen. His friends, riding with him in their car, watched as he nodded along, fingers tapping, overcome with emotion. Everyone in the car cried too. But it wasn’t all beauty. Now, he hears snippets of strangers’ conversations—the clatter of dishes, the buzz of a nearby TV—and it overwhelms him. 'I just want them to be quiet!' he laughs, sitting in a café, trying to tune out the chatter. Yet, the sound of a baby giggling? Pure magic. 'I never knew voices could sound like that,' he says, amazed. Chapman, now a freelance filmmaker, has spent years telling stories through images. His short films—like Eleven Eleven, which won top honors at film festivals—have earned acclaim for their visual storytelling. But now, he’s rewatching his own work, finally understanding the soundtracks others crafted. He dreams of making a feature film where he designs the audio himself. His journey began when he posted online asking for music recommendations. Within days, Reddit users sent over 14,000 suggestions—from Beethoven to the Beatles. He’s waiting to get a top-tier sound system before tackling the entire Beatles catalog. 'I want to really hear them,' he says with a grin. Experts say his reaction isn’t unusual. For adults who’ve lived without sound for decades, the first exposure can be overwhelming—a mix of joy, confusion, and awe. 'It’s like seeing a high-res photo for the first time,' he explains. And when asked how it feels? He smiles: 'It’s like the first time you kiss someone.'

article_content: At just 14 years old, Moshe Kai Cavalin is set to graduate with a degree in mathematics—having already completed college at age 11. Now, he faces a rare dilemma for a teenager: choosing between astrophysics and physics for his next degree. The Los Angeles native began reading college-level books at age two, a sign of his extraordinary intellect. His mother, Suichen Chein, recalls noticing his gifts early. After finishing his studies at East LA Community College at 11, he enrolled at UCLA, where his classmates—nearly a decade older—have warmly welcomed him. 'At first, they were curious—what was I doing there?' Moshe told ABC News. 'But then they started acting like big brothers and big sisters.' Today, he finds more comfort spending time with them than with peers his own age. Beyond academics, Moshe is a published author of 'We Can Do,' a book chronicling his journey. Yet he resists being labeled a 'genius.' 'Genius is just a word, like IQ is just a number,' he says. 'It labels you at one point and ignores everything else that makes you who you are.' His parents never forced him into advanced programs. His father, Joseph Cavalin, remembers seeing Moshe tutoring another child’s mother outside school—an experience that moved him to tears. When teachers suggested Moshe’s needs disrupted the classroom, his parents chose to enroll him in college at age eight—not out of pressure, but because he was ready. 'Happiness in childhood comes from loving parents and a creative environment,' Moshe says. His mother still accompanies him to class, but he insists his success stems from joy, not obligation. As he prepares for his next academic chapter, Moshe looks forward to summer activities: scuba diving and learning to drive. Though he’ll have to wait until he’s 16 for his license, he’s content to enjoy the journey—on his own terms.

article_content: Sir Cliff Richard has expressed deep anguish over what he describes as 'absurd and untrue allegations' of historical child sexual abuse, as police expand their investigation to include three alleged victims — both in the UK and abroad. The 74-year-old pop icon released a statement affirming his innocence, saying, 'I have never, in my life, assaulted anyone,' and expressing confidence that 'the truth will prevail.' He emphasized his full cooperation with authorities while criticizing the lack of direct communication from police. South Yorkshire Police confirmed the investigation — known as Operation Kaddie — has grown significantly since its inception, triggered by a 1985 allegation from a man now in his 40s who came forward through Operation Yewtree. Two additional complainants have since emerged. Police have not sent direct written updates to Cliff Richard, instead maintaining regular verbal briefings with his legal team every two weeks. This protocol, they say, is standard practice in active investigations. The case gained global attention after a highly publicized August 2014 raid on his Berkshire home, broadcast live by the BBC. Footage showed officers searching his property without charges having been filed. The incident drew widespread condemnation for breaches of privacy and investigative secrecy. An independent review led by former chief constable Andy Trotter found that South Yorkshire Police improperly shared confidential details with the BBC, including timing, location, and aerial imagery of the raid. A subsequent Metropolitan Police inquiry failed to identify the source of the leak. Cliff Richard, deeply affected by the media spectacle, has decided to sell his Sunningdale property, describing the experience as being 'ransacked by burglars.' He continues to thank supporters for their loyalty during what he calls an 'unbelievably difficult period.'

article_content: With a bang — that’s how George Strother described the start of his morning. In the early hours of Wednesday, a BMW sport utility vehicle crashed through the roof of the family’s garage in Escondido, California. 'My wife thought it was an earthquake — she was terrified,' Strother told reporters. Because their home sits below street level, an out-of-control vehicle could easily plunge onto the garage. 'The first thing we saw,' Strother said, 'was the BMW lying on the hood of our Nissan Pathfinder.' Emergency crews watched as a tow truck carefully extracted the SUV through the ceiling, dragging it across the driveway. 'There’s now a hole big enough to drive a BMW through,' Strother noted, though he believes the garage’s structure remains intact. According to Lt. Eric Skaja of the Escondido Police Department, the driver has not been found. The vehicle was a dealer loaner, and while the person to whom it was issued has been identified, they have not come forward or been arrested. Police are treating the incident as a misdemeanor hit-and-run. If the driver was intoxicated, Skaja emphasized, the penalties would be far more severe. Fortunately, the Strothers were never in danger — their bedroom is on the opposite side of the house.

article_content: After vanishing from his enclosure overnight, Rusty — a playful, year-old red panda at the Smithsonian National Zoo — was found safe and sound 24 hours later in the Adams Morgan neighborhood, just minutes from the zoo. Zoo staff had launched an urgent search, shutting down parts of the grounds and scanning every bush and rooftop, fearing the small animal might be injured, lost, or worse. Their worst fears eased when a local resident, Ashley Foughty, spotted Rusty darting through some shrubs near 20th and Biltmore Streets and snapped a photo, tweeting it to the zoo with a simple plea: 'Red panda in our neighborhood. Please come save him!' Within minutes, zoo personnel arrived and gently captured the dazed but unharmed panda. Rusty, who arrived from Lincoln, Nebraska, just weeks ago, had only recently begun appearing publicly to visitors. He was scheduled to eventually breed with the zoo’s female red panda, Shama. Though officials initially worried he might have escaped through faulty fencing or fallen ill, they confirmed he was healthy, vaccinated, and simply curious — perhaps drawn by unfamiliar smells beyond his enclosure. 'He’s not dangerous,' said spokesperson Pamela Baker-Masson. 'But if he feels trapped, he’ll defend himself.' The zoo praised the public’s quick thinking and thanked residents for their help. Rusty is now back in his habitat, resting and eating well again.

Nceda uyalela!' Ngokushesha, abaninzi bawo bayayibiza kanye nabafundi abakhulu bakho. Rusty, owasalela kwi-Lincoln, Nebraska, eminyakeni emine, awasemelane ngezinto eziningi emnyakeni. 'Awukho mthetho wakhe ku-umntu,' abonisa Pamela Baker-Masson. 'Kodwa ukuba uyakwazi ukuthi uyakwazi, uyayihamba.' Izinkulungwane zonke zazilalela izifundo zabo naye zazikhuluma ngokuvakalela. Rusty ayiphi kahle kuleli sitha, abandla kanye nesikhathi esifundiswayo.

article_content: On Sunday morning, a military bus carrying reservists from the Marine Corps overturned at Fort Rucker, an Army installation near Ozark, Alabama. The vehicle was transporting members of E Company, Anti-Terrorism Battalion, 4th Marine Division, who had just finished a training exercise. At approximately 9:20 a.m., the bus lost control and flipped, resulting in 23 service members being injured — four of whom were listed in critical condition. Most of the injured came from the First and Headquarters Platoons, based in Bessemer, Alabama, a suburb of Birmingham, with others hailing from Tallahassee, Florida. By midday, 11 of the wounded had been cleared to return to their unit after receiving medical care. The Department of Defense released images of the damaged bus to the press as part of its transparency effort. Ozark lies roughly 175 miles south of Birmingham.

Ngokushesha kwe-9:20 a.m., ubusi ubhalekile kwaye abaninzi abaningi ababili nezinto ezithile zikho — ezine zibe nezinyathelo eziningi. Abaningi abalapho baphele kwiFirst and Headquarters Platoons, e-Bessemer, Alabama, isikhundla se-Birmingham, nokho abaninzi abangaphandle e-Tallahassee, Florida. Ngokuphela kwemihla, izinyathelo ezine nasezantseni ezimbalwa ezinikezwa kwiqela. I-Department of Defense ayayiphatha izithombe zebhusi elilungileyo ekhaya kwi-media njengoko akho ukubambisana.

She is accused of not only engaging in sexual activity with the minor but also encouraging him to participate in such acts and exposing him to pornographic material. At her initial court appearance at Colchester Magistrates’ Court, McKay confirmed her details but did not enter a plea. Her case has now been transferred to Chelmsford Crown Court for trial early next year. She has been suspended from her role since May 2013, following the school’s receipt of the allegations. The Academies Enterprise Trust, which oversees the school, confirmed it has fully cooperated with police and social services throughout the investigation. Bail conditions prohibit any contact with the alleged victim. Neighbors described McKay as a quiet, friendly woman, expressing surprise at the charges. She lives with her third husband in a modest semi-detached home and has two adult daughters. No public comment has been made by McKay or her representatives.

article_content: White House Senior Adviser Dan Pfeiffer said today that he believes there is a real possibility House Republicans could move to impeach President Obama. Speaking at a Christian Science Monitor breakfast, Pfeiffer pointed to recent developments—including the House’s lawsuit against the president—as signs that impeachment, while still unlikely, is no longer unthinkable. 'I think a lot of people in this town laugh that off,' Pfeiffer said. 'But I would not discount that possibility.' He argued that Speaker John Boehner’s decision to pursue legal action against the president may inadvertently open the door to future impeachment discussions. Pfeiffer cited former Alaska Governor Sarah Palin’s public calls for impeachment and polling data showing majority support among Republicans as evidence that sentiment is shifting. 'Impeachment is a very serious constitutional tool,' he noted, 'and it’s been mentioned casually by figures like Palin and others without any credible allegations of wrongdoing.' Still, Pfeiffer warned that President Obama’s planned executive action on immigration could heighten tensions. 'If the president moves forward on immigration reform without Congress,' he said, 'it will certainly increase the likelihood that Republicans will consider impeachment. It would be foolish not to take that possibility seriously.' Republicans quickly pushed back. Boehner’s office condemned Pfeiffer’s comments as disingenuous, emphasizing the humanitarian crisis at the southern border, where more than 57,000 unaccompanied minors have arrived since October 2013. 'The White House is focused on political games instead of helping these children,' said Boehner aide Michael Steel. While a few GOP lawmakers, like retired Rep. Steve Stockman, have openly advocated for impeachment, no party leader has endorsed it. Boehner has repeatedly denied that the lawsuit is a stepping stone toward impeachment. Meanwhile, President Obama is set to meet with leaders from Guatemala, Honduras, and El Salvador to coordinate efforts to deter migration by clarifying that DACA does not apply to new arrivals.

article_content: Last week, a tragic collision in the Delaware River resulted in the sinking of a popular tourist boat, DUKW 34, claiming the lives of two teenage visitors from Hungary. Federal investigators from the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) revealed that the tour boat’s crew attempted to contact the nearby vessel Caribbean Sea — which was towing a large barge — via radio, but received no reply. Moments before the crash, the DUKW 34 had experienced mechanical trouble and was temporarily anchored in about 55 feet of water. At approximately 2:36 p.m., the barge struck the smaller vessel head-on, causing it to sink rapidly. Witnesses on other boats confirmed hearing the distress calls, though not all marine radio transmissions are recorded, complicating the investigation. One crew member aboard the Caribbean Sea chose not to speak with investigators, invoking their constitutional right against self-incrimination. In response, Ride The Ducks, the company operating the tour boat, expressed deep sorrow and reaffirmed its nearly two-decade safety record, noting no prior serious accidents since launching in 2003. The victims, 20-year-old Szabolcs Prem and 16-year-old Dora Schwendtner, were described as enthusiastic travelers enjoying a day on the river.

article_content: CNN reported that Algeria's president, Abdelaziz Bouteflika, was receiving treatment in France on Saturday for a 'mini-stroke,' according to medical and government officials cited by the state-run Algerian news agency. Prime Minister Abdelmalek Sellal told the Algerian Press Service that the president's condition was 'not serious.' The 76-year-old leader was transferred to a hospital in Paris for evaluation and care. Rachid Bougherbal, director of the National Center of Sports Medicine, stated there was 'no reason for worry' and that Bouteflika needed rest before undergoing further tests. First elected in 1999, Bouteflika has been pivotal to Algeria’s stability, guiding the nation through the end of its civil war, resisting Arab Spring unrest, and collaborating with Western nations against al Qaeda. He has publicly stated he will step down at the end of his current term next year. In recent years, Bouteflika has appeared rarely in public, sparking widespread speculation about his health. In 2005 and 2006, he received medical treatment in France for a stomach ailment, which led to rumors of stomach cancer. A 2011 U.S. diplomatic cable leaked by WikiLeaks claimed Bouteflika had cancer but was in remission. According to the Mayo Clinic, a 'mini-stroke' is medically termed a transient ischemic attack (TIA)—it mimics stroke symptoms but typically causes no lasting damage. The clinic warns that TIA may serve as a warning sign: about one in three people who experience a TIA will later suffer a full stroke.

U-Prime Minister Abdelmalek Sellal wayebonga i-Algerian Press Service ukuthi indlela yoko yayingenziwa ngokukhawuleza. Umhlaba o-76 uBouteflika ukuqhubeka ekhaya elungenileyo eParis kuqhubeka nokubuyela. Uyayiqhubeka nge-1999, uBouteflika uyisilungu saseAljeria, ukuze akhangelise amaqembu ephendulekileyo, ukuze akhulume ne-Arab Spring, kwaye ukuze akhangele nge-Western nations ngokuthi akhulume ne-al Qaeda. Ngokwe-Mayo Clinic, 'mini-stroke' iyisithelo esikhathini esikhulu (TIA)—inezantsi ezifana ne-stroke kodwa ayikho ukusapha. article_content: Rita Baci, a 65-year-old kindergarten teacher at John E. Ford Montessori School in Duval County, Florida, has been suspended without pay following an investigation into serious misconduct. According to the Duval County Schools investigative report, Baci allegedly recorded multiple incidents in which one child violently assaulted other students—hitting them about the face and body, kicking a child hiding under a table, and punching another—using her cellphone camera on at least three occasions. She reportedly failed to intervene during these events. Additionally, investigators found that Baci pushed a student out of the classroom with her foot and left him unattended. The videos were later shown to other students and a vice principal prior to a meeting with the affected child’s parents. School officials concluded that Baci violated the district’s code of ethics by failing to make a reasonable effort to protect students from harm. Baci, who teaches multiple subjects using the Montessori method with students with emotional disabilities, remains suspended pending further review.

article_content: The horrifying ordeal endured by 89-year-old Edna Slann at the struggling Grantley Court care home was revealed last night through harrowing video footage. In the recording, taken by her granddaughter in September, a frail and visibly distressed Edna pleads: 'I'm starving — they keep you starving in here. I just want a cup of tea. Do you have anything to eat?' According to The Mail, a ten-week stay at Grantley Court left Edna severely malnourished, bruised, and suffering from an infection doctors say will likely be fatal within weeks. Detectives are investigating unexplained injuries suffered by other dementia patients at the home, which has since been closed, alongside Merok Park in Banstead, Surrey. Both facilities were owned by multimillionaires Soondressen and Maleenee Cooppen. When asked by The Mail to apologize to families, 42-year-old Mrs. Cooppen responded: 'We are not interested.' Families reacted with fury, vowing legal action. 'It is disgusting,' said Edna’s daughter, Linda Cackett. 'Clearly, they don’t care at all. You can see how desperate my mother was. If I were them, I wouldn’t be able to sleep at night.' Edna, a widow with dementia and arthritis, was moved to Grantley Court in July from another residential home. Her family noticed rapid decline: she lost over half a stone in two months, now weighs just over five stone, and requires morphine for pain. She sustained a head injury requiring 12 stitches and severe bruising. Inspectors found an overpowering smell of urine, patients forced to bathe in cold water, and grossly inadequate staffing. Neighbors reported hearing screams and cries for help. Two residents died shortly after emergency evacuations: an 85-year-old man 48 hours after Merok Park’s closure in December, and 91-year-old Winifred Lake two weeks after leaving Grantley Court. Despite red flags, both homes passed inspections less than a year prior — with concerns about staff training and vetting at Grantley Court suppressed for eight months due to an alleged administrative delay. The Cooppens, who reside in a £2.5 million home on a gated estate in Cheam, own multiple luxury vehicles including a £70,000 Mercedes S350, a £50,000 BMW X5, and a £30,000 BMW convertible. They also own a £500,000 property in Sutton they rent out. Their children lead extravagant lives: their 20-year-old daughter Davina celebrated her 18th birthday with a luxury party in Mauritius, arriving in a limousine and drinking champagne. Their 16-year-old son, Arvin, posts online photos of designer watches, expensive jewelry, and the family’s two racehorses. On Christmas Eve, he shared images of Dom Perignon and high-end spirits. Edna’s care cost £595 per week, funded by Surrey Downs Clinical Commissioning Group. The CCG stated she was relocated immediately once concerns were raised. Surrey County Council noted that at the time of her admission, Grantley Court had recently passed inspection. The Home Office is investigating whether staff at Merok Park were working illegally in the UK. The Metropolitan Police confirm investigations are ongoing.

article_content: On Monday, Tommy Robinson — known for leading the far-right English Defence League — visited Selfridges on Oxford Street with a friend who intended to purchase jeans. According to Robinson, a store employee refused to serve his companion, shouting, 'F*** off, I'm not serving you.' Robinson captured the exchange on video and later posted it online, identifying the staff member as a Muslim and questioning whether the refusal stemmed from his own affiliation with the EDL. He insisted his friend had done nothing wrong and was merely accompanying him. Following the complaint, Selfridges management invited Robinson and his friend to enjoy a complimentary three-course meal at their upscale Hix Restaurant. The bill totaled £83 and included prawn cocktail (£11.25), steak with béarnaise sauce (£25), and chocolate cake with ice cream (£5.25). Robinson shared photos of the meal on Twitter, praising the store’s 'top lad' manager and calling the gesture 'complimentary lunch, couldn't be more apologetic.' The employee involved was briefly suspended but later reinstated after an internal review. Selfridges issued a statement reaffirming its longstanding commitment to serving all customers, regardless of background, and emphasized the staff member’s long tenure with the company. However, the decision to offer a free luxury meal sparked widespread criticism. Many shoppers took to social media to express disgust, labeling Selfridges as 'a disgrace' for rewarding someone with a history of violent and extremist associations. Others defended the store, applauding the reinstatement of the employee and criticizing those who called for his dismissal. The incident has ignited debate over how businesses should respond to conflict, discrimination claims, and public relations missteps.

article_content: A former soldier has admitted to tying a pig’s head to the gates of a mosque and spray-painting racist graffiti. Simon Parkes, 45, attached the severed head to the front of Cheltenham Mosque in Gloucestershire and daubed offensive messages nearby. His actions were deeply offensive to Muslims, who regard pigs and pork consumption as unclean. He evaded justice for nearly two years until police arrested him in July 2012 for this crime and an unrelated offense. Parkes, of Bishops Cleeve in Cheltenham, appeared at Cheltenham Magistrates’ Court and pleaded guilty to racially aggravated criminal damage and a public order offense. He is scheduled to be sentenced at Gloucester Crown Court later this month. The pig’s head was left at the mosque on November 13, 2010. A spokesperson for Cheltenham Mosque said: 'This was a profoundly shocking incident—not only for mosque attendees but for the entire community. We are incredibly grateful to the police, the local council, and our neighbors for their overwhelming support.' 'We are thankful that the damage was repaired quickly, allowing everyone to return to normal life as soon as possible.' Gloucestershire Police described Parkes’ arrest as the result of a 'painstaking and difficult' investigation. Inspector Tim Waterhouse said: 'Though this disturbing incident occurred nearly two years ago, a determined and thorough inquiry led to Parkes’ conviction. The message is clear: commit a crime in Cheltenham at your peril—we will not relent in our efforts to protect our communities and bring offenders to justice.'

article_content: At the 2012 Scottish Fashion Awards in Glasgow’s Clyde Auditorium, Alexa Chung hosted the event in a standout outfit from Christopher Kane’s Spring/Summer 2012 collection: an oversized white shirt paired with a floral silk dress and tan suede brogues. True to her signature aesthetic, she embodied effortless elegance. Kane, a 29-year-old Central Saint Martins graduate, took home the prestigious title of Scottish Fashion Designer of the Year, defeating two-time winner Jonathan Saunders. In his acceptance speech, he expressed deep gratitude, highlighting Scotland’s rich creative ecosystem: 'Scotland has such a wealth of great fashion talent—from design to production. It’s something we should all be proud of.' Other notable attendees included Doctor Who star Karen Gillan—named Scottish Fashion Icon—who dazzled in a bold yellow-and-black mini dress, and supermodel Stella Tennant, inducted into the Hall of Fame. David Gandy, face of Dolce & Gabbana, and Sugababe Jade Ewan also graced the red carpet. Tali Lennox, daughter of Annie Lennox, won Scottish Model of the Year for the second year running. Meanwhile, Hayley Scanlan was honored as Scottish Young Designer of the Year, and William Chambers took home the Accessory Designer award. International acclaim went to Mulberry, named International Designer of the Year for incorporating Scottish fabric, and Dashing Tweeds, crowned Scottish Textile Brand of the Year. The evening featured live performances by Dionne Bromfield—Amy Winehouse’s goddaughter—and rising Scottish teen artist Tallia Storm, who had recently performed for Elton John. Bromfield chose a fringe-hemmed dress by fellow Scot Holly Fulton, a nominee for Designer of the Year, saying: 'I’d never have been offered these designers in London.' article_content: Dr. Sue Downing, a veterinarian known for treating Hollywood stars like Benicio del Toro and Katherine McPhee, is desperately searching for her two beloved dogs after a burglary at her Los Angeles home. Spice, a three-year-old terrier born with a mobility condition, and Penny, a thirteen-year-old Pomeranian managing a serious heart ailment, vanished during the break-in. Though nothing else was taken from her Culver City residence—even though the place was thoroughly ransacked—Downing fears the dogs were specifically targeted. Neither dog was wearing a collar at the time, though both are microchipped. Downing, who also serves as a commissioner at the Los Angeles Zoo, says she isn’t sure whether the intruders stole them or accidentally left the gate open, allowing the animals to escape. Still, she’s terrified for their safety: both require daily medication and are unusually dependent on her care. 'I’ve checked every corner of my yard, every neighbor’s fence,' she told KTLA 5. 'They’re gentle, loving, and completely helpless without me. I just want them home.' To aid the search, she’s offering a $500 reward and has circulated photos widely. 'I don’t care about my stuff,' she said. 'My dogs are my family. If someone has them, please, just let me know—they need their medicine.' Authorities and the public are now urged to keep an eye out, as Downing worries the dogs could be sold to unsuspecting buyers unaware of their medical needs.

article_content: Caroline Kennedy, the U.S. Ambassador to Japan, has softly signaled that she would 'absolutely' back Hillary Clinton if Clinton decides to run for president in 2016. Though the two come from powerhouse Democratic families and have been allies for decades, their relationship hit a major snag in 2008 when Kennedy threw her weight behind Barack Obama—a move widely credited with helping shift the Democratic primary in Obama’s favor. At the time, Clinton’s supporters were furious, accusing Kennedy of being politically inactive and even neglecting to vote. But Clinton herself stepped in, telling her followers to back off. Now, with speculation swirling about whether Clinton will enter the 2016 race, Kennedy offered a carefully worded comment: 'Two years is a really long time in politics... I hope so.' Her phrasing leaves room for doubt, especially since Clinton hasn’t officially declared. Some analysts wonder if Kennedy might be keeping her own options open—perhaps eyeing a presidential bid of her own, continuing the Kennedy legacy left unfinished by her father, JFK. Meanwhile, Kennedy took the opportunity during an ABC interview to praise President Obama’s leadership in Asia, defending his record even as other Democrats grow distant. She called him a president who thinks long-term and truly advances American interests.

article_content: BP has asked a judge to temporarily halt economic loss-based compensation payments related to the Deepwater Horizon oil spill. The settlement, one of the largest in U.S. history, initially allocated $7.8 billion. The 2010 explosion on the Deepwater Horizon rig killed 11 workers and ruptured the Macondo well, spilling an estimated 4 million barrels of oil into the Gulf of Mexico — the worst offshore oil spill in U.S. history. The well took 84 days to seal. BP has launched an appeal against what it calls 'fictitious' and 'absurd' compensation payouts, requesting a temporary pause on payments made to businesses based on alleged economic losses. In a New Orleans court filing, BP cited examples of companies far from the spill zone — including a rice mill 40 miles inland in Louisiana and a construction firm nearly 200 miles away in northern Alabama — that reported higher profits in 2010 yet still received millions in compensation. The British oil giant, which has already sold $38 billion in assets to fund compensation, cleanup, and fines, warns that ongoing payouts could exceed its original $42 billion reserve, causing 'irreparable harm.' Although BP agreed to a $7.8 billion settlement in April 2012, the actual payout is uncapped and determined by court-appointed administrator Patrick Juneau under complex eligibility rules. Claimants may calculate losses by comparing any three consecutive months in 2010 with any comparable period between January 2007 and December 2009 — a method BP argues allows inflated or unfounded claims. Despite these concerns, over 100,000 individuals and businesses — including fishermen, restaurant owners, and tourism operators — received compensation for livelihood and health impacts. BP has already committed $37 billion and faces potential additional liabilities beyond its 2012 agreement to pay $4.5 billion to resolve criminal charges.

article_content: A police inquiry has been launched into the deaths of several patients treated by colorectal surgeon Sudip Sarker. Police are investigating at least three deaths of NHS patients who underwent surgery by Sarker, a cancer specialist. According to a report by the Royal College of Surgeons (RCS), Sarker had twice the death rate of comparable surgeons during his tenure as a consultant general surgeon at Worcester Royal Hospital and the Alexandra Hospital in Redditch. One in five of his patients required readmission following procedures. Concerns about his work as a colon and bowel keyhole surgery specialist were raised by colleagues in July 2012, leading to a referral to the RCS. Despite ongoing investigations, Sarker continued performing surgeries for several months—without patients’ knowledge—until he was suspended in October 2012. He remains excluded from his post in Worcestershire, a position he held since August 2011, and the General Medical Council has imposed restrictions on his license to practice. A patient support hotline was only established by Worcestershire Acute Hospitals NHS Trust in June 2023. A coroner was scheduled to hold a joint inquest into the 2012 deaths of three patients: William Jones (84), Daphne Taylor (81), and Jean Thomas (80), but the hearing has been adjourned pending the police investigation. Superintendent Kevin Purcell confirmed that West Mercia Police received a formal complaint in December 2013 and are now reviewing whether other patient deaths may be linked. The NHS Trust acted promptly upon learning of potential issues by commissioning the RCS review, which found Sarker’s mortality and readmission rates were significantly elevated. Hundreds of patients who underwent major bowel cancer procedures have been recalled for reassessment, and a separate review is underway for all patients who had any contact with Sarker—even for minor treatments. Dozens of complaints have been filed, and some families have retained legal counsel. Inez Brown of the Medical Accident Group stated: 'The victims who have come forward may be just the tip of the iceberg. His actions impacted hundreds, if not thousands, of families. Early cancer detection saves lives, yet he repeatedly failed to achieve this. The police investigation suggests this goes beyond negligence.' It is understood Sarker continues to receive his full £85,000 annual salary. A spokesperson for the NHS Trust stated: 'As soon as a potential problem was identified, we acted swiftly and responsibly to protect patients. An expert multidisciplinary team has reviewed all records of patients who underwent major operations. At-risk patients were recalled for further evaluation. A separate review of all patients who had contact with Mr. Sarker is being conducted by external surgical specialists.'

article_content: United Airlines announced on Monday that it will not resume flights from Newark, New Jersey, to Tel Aviv, Israel, on November 24, as previously planned. The airline apologized for the confusion, attributing the earlier announcement of resumption to an error by its public relations agency. Several media outlets, including Reuters, had reported the planned restart based on the PR agency’s initial statement. United confirmed that its Tel Aviv flights will remain suspended until conditions permit safe operations. The suspension follows a wave of flight reductions by U.S. carriers after the October 7 Hamas attack triggered heightened security concerns across the Middle East. Among U.S. airlines, United has the most extensive presence on the Tel Aviv route, with services typically operating from major hubs like New York, Chicago, Washington, and Miami. On Monday morning, United Airlines shares dipped 0.6%.

article_content: The UK Ministry of Defence has confirmed it will deploy sonic weapons called Long Range Acoustic Devices (LRADs) during the 2012 London Olympics and the upcoming UEFA European Football Championship. These devices, manufactured in the United States, produce extremely loud, targeted sound waves — up to 150 decibels — enough to cause physical discomfort and compel crowds to disperse. But they’re not just noisemakers: LRADs can also broadcast clear verbal instructions, such as 'please move back' or 'disperse now.' Recent tests conducted by the MoD on the River Thames showed the devices mounted on Royal Marine vessels, simulating crowd control scenarios. Footage from past uses — including a G20 protest in the U.S. — shows people instinctively covering their ears and fleeing the intense noise. While the MoD insists these tools will be used mainly as 'loudspeakers' rather than weapons, critics point out their history: the U.S. military has deployed them in Iraq and against pirate vessels off Somalia. Their directional design allows security teams to focus the sound on specific groups, minimizing unintended exposure. This move is part of a wider security push ahead of the Games, which already sparked debate after officials announced surface-to-air missiles would be installed on rooftops of residential buildings near the Olympic Stadium — including Bow Quarter, home to 700 families. The MoD says all equipment is being used to support police-led efforts to ensure public safety during a high-risk event.

Izinto ezifakazi e-Amerika zazithatha imithi yama-150, ezinokubonisa ukuthi abantu baphindwa noma bazalisa izimpendulo ezingenamandla amazwi, njengoko 'hamba nje' noma 'lalela.' article_content: Richard Montañez didn’t start with a degree, a suit, or even fluent English—he started with a mop and a bold idea. In 1976, working as a janitor at a Frito-Lay plant in Rancho Cucamonga, California, he noticed a batch of Cheetos had come out without cheese due to a broken machine. Taking some home, he sprinkled chili powder on them—and loved the result. Encouraged by his family and coworkers, he dared to pitch the concept to the company’s top executives. With no tie and only a library book on marketing to guide him, he walked into the boardroom and changed his life forever. The snack became Flamin’ Hot Cheetos, now one of Frito-Lay’s best-selling products. But his impact went beyond snacks. Montañez became a symbol of what’s possible when you refuse to be limited by your title. Today, as Executive Vice President of Multicultural Sales and Community Activation at PepsiCo North America, he speaks at major events, advises MBA students, and travels the world in corporate jets. He often recalls being mocked in school for bringing a burrito instead of a bologna sandwich. His mother’s advice? ‘This is who you are.’ She gave him two burritos the next day and told him to make a friend. By the end of the week, he was selling them for 25 cents each. Now, he gives back—funding scholarships, feeding families, and reminding companies: ‘There’s no such thing as just a janitor. If you act like an owner, you are one.’

Kodwa ukuze kuhleleke kakhulu kakhulu. U-Montañez ubonakala njengefaniso yendlela efana ngesikhathi esifuna ukusetyenziswa ngokwemigaqo. Njengemihla yekhaya yaseNingizimu Afrika, u-Executive Vice President of Multicultural Sales and Community Activation kwi-PepsiCo North America, uyakwazi ukubona imihla, ukufunda abafundi baMBA, nokuthi uyahamba kahle kahle kwi-jets zokhaya. article_content: Paul Walker, the beloved actor known for his role in the Fast & Furious films, passed away on November 30, 2013, following a devastating car crash in Santa Clarita, California. According to his official death certificate, released publicly for the first time, his death resulted from the combined effects of severe physical trauma and thermal injuries — meaning he suffered fatal burns in addition to blunt force trauma. His friend and the car’s driver, Roger Rodas, also died instantly in the same incident, though his certificate listed only traumatic injuries, with no reference to burns. The two men were traveling home from a charity event when their 2005 Porsche Carrera GT lost control, veered off the road, and ignited in flames. Due to the intensity of the fire, both bodies were too badly damaged for visual identification, and dental records were used to confirm their identities. Investigators are still examining what caused the crash, with some experts suggesting that small, raised road markers called Botts’ Dots may have contributed to hydroplaning under wet conditions. The release of the documents coincided with a heartfelt memorial service held on a beach in Santa Barbara, where Walker’s family, including his 15-year-old daughter Meadow and 25-year-old brother Cody, along with his parents, gathered to remember him. They spent the afternoon laughing, playing football, and enjoying the sunshine — a quiet, personal tribute to a man they loved. Tyrese Gibson, Walker’s co-star from the Fast & Furious series, was also present, honoring his friend’s memory alongside others who knew him best.

Kukhona isifundo sesithuthi sasekuphakeme, esiboniswe kakhulu ngenyanga yonke, ukuthi ukuqala kwezinkinga ezimbili zombili zokuthula nezinkulungwane ezinene. Bafunda, bafunda ifutbhalu, bafunda izinsuku ezinene — isifundo esilungileyo esinikezwe kumntwana othetha. Tyrese Gibson, umntwana othetha naye kwi-Fast & Furious, abonakala kakhulu, akhusela isiphumo sikaPaul.

article_content: Jeremy Meeks, widely known as the 'hot felon,' was sentenced to 27 months in federal prison on Thursday for being a felon in possession of a firearm, according to CBS News. His arrest in June of the previous year followed felony weapon charges, and his mugshot—featuring striking baby blue eyes and a chiseled jawline—quickly went viral across social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, and Tumblr. Thousands online praised his appearance, dubbing him nicknames such as 'Hotty McMug Shot' and 'Mugshot McDreamy,' and popularizing hashtags like #FelonCrushFriday. Yet many overlooked his extensive criminal history, which spans over a decade and includes charges of grand larceny and identity theft. The presiding judge showed little leniency, imposing the 27-month sentence alongside 500 hours in a Bureau of Prisons Substance Abuse Treatment Program. A $100 fine was ordered but waived due to Meeks’ inability to pay. Though Meeks had reportedly secured a modeling contract with a Santa Monica-based agency, his incarceration effectively ends any immediate prospects for a modeling career. His next photograph will not be a high-fashion shoot—but a federal prison mugshot.

article_content: After a chaotic recount, the Iowa Republican Party officially certified Rick Santorum as the winner of the 2012 caucuses by just 34 votes over Mitt Romney — reversing the initial report that had given Romney an 8-vote edge. Though the results were updated days later, eight precincts’ votes remain missing forever, meaning the true winner may never be fully confirmed. Santorum celebrated the corrected tally as a hard-won upset, telling CNN he felt ‘very, very good’ about overcoming Romney in the state where he was expected to lose. Romney, in response, called the outcome a ‘virtual tie,’ thanked Iowa Republicans for their diligence, and congratulated Santorum without conceding. Campaign aides clashed over whether Romney had called to concede; Santorum’s team said yes, while Romney’s team insisted it was merely a courtesy call. The revised result shattered the narrative that Romney had swept the first two contests, injecting fresh energy into Santorum’s campaign just before the critical South Carolina primary. Santorum’s strategist Hogan Gidley declared the win a ‘landslide in Iowa,’ noting how it disrupted the idea of Romney as unbeatable. Meanwhile, Romney remained steady, pointing to his decisive New Hampshire win and positioning himself as the consistent frontrunner. Despite the drama, experts like CNN’s Candy Crowley noted the vote difference was too small to meaningfully alter the broader race — though Santorum now had the moral high ground and media buzz. With South Carolina voting in two days and record turnout expected, both campaigns scrambled to frame the moment as pivotal — one side calling it redemption, the other calling it noise.

Kodwa kusukela kule nqanaba, i-zithi zomlomo azikho 8 ezifunekayo, kodwa akukho ukuthi uyisiphi umntu oqala. Abaphawuli abaningi bakhuluma ngokuthi u-Romney ayihamba ekhaya kuyabonga; abaphawuli baka-Santorum bayazama ukuthi yaye, kodwa abaphawuli baka-Romney bayazama ukuthi kuyafana nezinye izindlela. Ukulungiselela kwezinye izinto ezithile ezinamaphuzu abonakale kakhulu, nokuthi u-Romney ayikho ukuthi abonakele kwi-Iowa kanye ne-New Hampshire, nokuthi u-Santorum uyakwenzeka kakhulu. Kodwa u-Romney ayikho ukuthi abonakele, ukuze ufake inkundla yabo kwi-New Hampshire, nokuthi uyisiphi sasemthethweni. Nangona kuyacala, abaphawuli abanengi njenge-CNN u-Candy Crowley bakhuluma ukuthi ukudala kwezinye izinto ezithile azikho ukuthi kuyahlakanipha indlela yobubanzi — kodwa u-Santorum uya kuba nesikhathi esikhulu nasekupheleni. Kanti u-South Carolina ubuyela kule sithi, kanti i-zithi zomlomo ziyahlukene, abaphawuli abaningi bakhuluma ukuthi kuyisiphi sasemthethweni — one side calling it redemption, the other calling it noise.

article_content: Bobbi Kristina Houston, the 21-year-old daughter of the late Whitney Houston, was found unconscious in a bathtub at her Georgia home on January 31, 2015, and has remained in a medically induced coma at Emory University Hospital in Atlanta ever since. Doctors were unable to safely wake her from the coma after she experienced seizures during medication reduction, prompting medical staff to maintain sedation. She underwent a tracheotomy last week and continues to be on life support. Few official updates about her condition have been released. Her father, R&B singer Bobby Brown, has requested that the media refrain from interviewing family members who have spoken publicly about her health. Tensions have escalated between Bobbi Kristina’s boyfriend, Nick Gordon, and Bobby Brown. Gordon posted a series of emotional Twitter messages accusing Brown of neglecting his daughter for years and seeking financial gain from Whitney Houston’s estate. Gordon claimed he had cared for Bobbi Kristina and her mother full-time since Whitney’s death in 2012, and alleged that Brown had visited his daughter only four times in five years. He also expressed regret for not administering CPR sooner on the night she was found, and insisted she would hate her father when she awakens. Attorneys for Bobby Brown stated Gordon was offered the chance to visit Bobbi Kristina—but only if he provided a written account of what occurred the night of the incident. Gordon’s legal team says he repeatedly offered to speak privately, but Brown refused. Police in Roswell, Georgia, are investigating whether suspicious injuries on Bobbi Kristina’s body suggest foul play. Gordon is considered a person of interest. Reports indicate Bobbi Kristina had been using cocaine, heroin, and Xanax in the months leading up to the incident, and was reportedly distraught over her mother’s death. Four days before the bathtub incident, she was involved in a serious car crash in which another driver sustained critical injuries. Her vehicle’s tire had been punctured by a nail and failed. Although Gordon and Bobbi Kristina referred to each other as husband and wife, they were never legally married. Bobby Brown has denied any romantic relationship between them.

article_content: A handyman has been sentenced to 10 years in prison after accidentally killing his girlfriend with a homemade cannon. Richard Fox, 41, an explosives enthusiast, was loading the device at his trailer home in Petrero — a small mountain community near California’s border with Mexico — when it detonated unexpectedly. Shrapnel from the blast pierced the trailer wall, instantly killing his girlfriend, Jeanette Ogara, 38. Their four-year-old daughter, Vanessa, was unharmed. Fox pleaded guilty to felony charges related to the unlawful explosion of a destructive device and possession of materials intended for such use. Prosecutors accepted his claim that he never intended to cause harm. The accident occurred on March 3, 2012, when Fox and a friend were outside the trailer, consuming alcohol while filling the cannon with black powder extracted from fireworks, along with 'salutes' and tightly packed aluminum foil. According to testimony by retired detective Robert Luke, the foil blocked airflow, preventing safe ignition and causing catastrophic pressure buildup. The explosion severely burned Fox and scattered metal fragments across the area. Multiple pieces of shrapnel struck the trailer, killing Ogara instantly. The child and three other adults inside were unharmed. Fox broke down in tears during sentencing at the El Cajon branch of the San Diego County Superior Court, begging the family for forgiveness. 'I am truly sorry from the bottom of my heart,' he told the LA Times. Neighbors described Fox as a curious tinkerer who enjoyed disassembling and reassembling mechanical objects. John Arnold, a neighbor, said, 'He liked experimenting with guns — and it looks like this experiment went bad.' Fox’s brother Jerry said his sibling had 'always lived on the edge,' adding, 'They mean the world to him. I can’t imagine how he feels right now.' After the explosion, Fox called his brother and said, 'I’m sorry, I’m sorry, it should have been me.' He was hospitalized for shrapnel wounds to his right leg and later arrested. Fox had a prior criminal record, including a 1990s prison term for vehicle theft and weapon possession. Judge Patricia Cookson cited this history as a reason to impose the maximum sentence. Fox will receive credit for the two years he spent in custody awaiting trial.

article_content: In a disturbing yet unusual incident in southern British Columbia, a black bear was found to have interacted with the body of Rory Nelson Wagner, a 53-year-old man who had been convicted of murder. Authorities from the Royal Canadian Mounted Police discovered Wagner’s remains near his parked 1986 Volkswagen Jetta, where the bear had apparently entered through the open driver’s window. Evidence such as muddy paw prints and claw marks on the vehicle suggested the bear had scavenged portions of the body and dragged the rest approximately 120 meters into the surrounding forest. Inside the car, police found drug paraphernalia and an empty liquor bottle, indicating Wagner may have died from causes unrelated to violence. Wagner, who was on parole, had been sentenced in 1993 for the killing of a man who had been acquitted of sexually assaulting Wagner’s relative. While the bear has been captured, conservation officials are evaluating whether it poses a continued risk to public safety — a decision that could lead to its euthanasia. An autopsy and toxicology report are pending to determine the exact cause of Wagner’s death.

article_content: People in five areas of the UK must now dial the full area code to call local homes and businesses, as regulators warn that landline numbers are running out. The change, effective Wednesday, applies to Aberdeen (01224), Bradford (01274), Brighton (01273), Middlesbrough (01642), and Milton Keynes (01908). Callers must include the area code—even for local calls—just as they would when dialing a mobile number. If they forget, they will hear a recorded message prompting them to redial with the full code. The move, implemented by telecoms regulator Ofcom, aims to generate nearly one million new landline numbers by enabling prefixes beginning with 0 or 1, previously restricted to avoid confusion with existing dialing codes (e.g., 07 for mobiles, 08 for premium rates, 118 for directory enquiries). Ofcom claims the transition is straightforward and cites Bournemouth’s smooth 2012 rollout as proof. Call costs remain unchanged. Similar changes are planned for Oxford, Slough, and Stoke-on-Trent in the years following 2016, with contingency plans for up to 20 additional cities—including Swindon, Hull, York, Norwich, Guildford, Warwick, Bath, and Motherwell. However, public skepticism persists. With growing reliance on mobile phones and internet-based services like Skype, demand for new landline numbers is declining. Critics argue the change imposes unnecessary burdens: households must remember longer 11-digit numbers, and small businesses face costs to update signage and stationery. Ofcom maintains the reform safeguards future number availability and prevents more disruptive measures, such as reassigning existing numbers. It also argues that expanded numbering supports competition among telecom providers, benefiting consumers.

article_content: In the wake of her husband’s tragic death, Stephanie Madoff Mack has spoken out for the first time, placing full blame on Bernie Madoff for destroying her family. Mark Madoff, Bernie’s son, took his own life in December 2010—two years after his father’s arrest for orchestrating a $60 billion fraud. Stephanie says Mark was shattered by the scandal, watching helplessly as his father’s lies unraveled, growing a beard to hide his face and even attempting suicide in 2009 with a note that read: 'F**k you, Dad.' Now 37 and raising two young children—Audrey, 4, and Nicholas, 2—Stephanie describes how Mark’s laughter vanished overnight. In her upcoming memoir, 'The End Of Normal,' she writes that the man she fell in love with disappeared beneath the weight of shame and fear. She recalls Audrey crying out to the sky, 'I love you, Daddy,' and asking why he didn’t take his phone when he died. Stephanie has refused to forgive her mother-in-law, Ruth Madoff, whom she accuses of abandoning Mark after choosing to return to Bernie following a 2009 prison assault. Ruth was barred from Mark’s funeral. Stephanie also holds Andrew Madoff accountable for turning away from his brother during his darkest hours. Though once part of the same family, Stephanie’s wedding video—filmed in 2004—shows a joyful scene: Bernie escorting Ruth to her seat, Stephanie walking down the aisle in white, dancing with her new husband and even sharing a disco dance with her future father-in-law. Now, those images feel like relics of a life that never was. Stephanie has changed her name to distance herself from the scandal and is focused on rebuilding her life without deceit. 'I want to live without lies, betrayal, or sorrow,' she told ABC News. Her story is not just about loss—it’s about survival.

article_content: Bengaluru: Seasoned cueist Vidya Pillai gifted herself an early birthday present—the one she had been chasing for over a decade. After six failed attempts in world championship finals, Vidya, who turns 46 on Sunday, finally claimed the World title. This is the first individual world snooker title won by an Indian woman. The Bengaluru-based player delivered a stellar performance, defeating all opponents en route to victory at the IBSF 6-Red Snooker World Championship in Doha, Qatar, on Friday night. In the final, Vidya outplayed fellow Indian Anupama Ramachandran 4–1. "It hasn’t sunk in yet. So many people are so happy for me. I’m completely at a loss for words," Vidya told The Times of India shortly after her win. "It’s been a long wait—so many finals, so many close matches. But this one is special. I had a tough half: Ng On Yee of Hong Kong in the quarterfinals, Bai Yulu of China in the semis. Beating two world champions back-to-back feels incredible." Apart from her semifinal battle with Yulu, Vidya sailed through the tournament. She topped Group A with a perfect record and cruised past compatriot Varshaa Sanjeev 3–0 in the pre-quarters. Her quarterfinal opponent, Ng On Yee, was outclassed 4–0. Vidya posted a 33-run break in the second frame and a blistering 63 clearance in the fourth. On Yee managed just 15 points across the entire match. Vidya, who lost to Yulu in the 15-red semifinal just four days prior, started poorly in the semis, trailing 0–2. But displaying her trademark grit, she leveled the score and clinched the decider by potting the final two reds and all the colors. In the final, Anupama offered brief resistance but was no match for Vidya’s consistency. Vidya had lost both the 15-red and 6-red finals last year from winning positions in Turkey. Those near-misses might have broken others—but not her. "Hope is something we all live with," Vidya said after her heartbreaking loss to On Yee in the Eden World Women’s Snooker Championship in Singapore. "I never gave up hope." "This year has been incredible—I won two national pool titles, a gold at the National Games, a bronze in the 15-red Worlds four days ago, and now this gold, which is very, very special," she concluded. Vidya also played a pivotal role in Asia B’s triumph at the WCBS Team Championship in Ankara in July.

article_content: Photographer Andy Lee has captured a series of haunting images showcasing some of the world’s most breathtaking roads. His work includes routes through the Snæfellsnes Peninsula in Iceland, the Lake District in England, the Hebrides in Scotland, and Northern Ireland’s iconic Dark Hedges — a tree-lined avenue famously used as a filming location for Game of Thrones. The Dark Hedges, planted by the Stuart family in the 18th century, were designed as a grand entrance feature to Gracehill House, their Georgian mansion. Today, they are among the most photographed natural landmarks in Northern Ireland. Lee’s series, titled 'Roads,' also features striking black-and-white images from West Iceland, including 'Road to the South, Iceland,' and scenes from the Isle of Skye and Pembrokeshire. The 100-kilometre-long Snæfellsnes Peninsula is renowned for its fjords, volcanic peaks, dramatic sea cliffs, and the glimmering ice cap Snæfellsjökull — a landmark immortalized in Jules Verne’s Journey to the Centre of the Earth. Welsh-born Lee, who works as a filmmaker, photographer, and painter, began taking photography seriously about ten years ago while filming a documentary for a charity in Ethiopia. Carrying an old Hasselblad film camera between scenes, he began photographing everything around him. 'From that moment on, I was hooked,' he says. 'The joy I still get from seeing an image projected onto ground glass, or the smell of developer, is enough to keep me shooting with a smile on my face.' He draws inspiration from Jack Kerouac’s On the Road: 'There was nowhere to go but everywhere.' Lee adds, 'Getting lost is half the fun.' While he loves portraiture, he has recently grown drawn to landscape photography — and hopes to combine both in future projects.

I-Dark Hedges, ezifakazile ngamakhulu kaStuart eminyakeni engu-18, ziyaziwa njengesikwele esivumelwe ukuphila kwiGracehill House, yimoto yeGeorgian. article_content: WASHINGTON (CNN) — Even as FEMA rushes sandbags, generators, and pumps to the flooded Midwest, a government report questions the agency’s ability to distribute relief supplies effectively during major disasters. Field employees at the Federal Emergency Management Agency still rely on ad hoc computer systems—and in some cases, paper forms—to order and distribute goods, according to a report released Tuesday. Cots, tarps, and other items donated by external agencies and charities are not easily integrated into FEMA’s supply chain, the report found. Field personnel have placed duplicate orders for disaster supplies because some of FEMA’s computer systems do not communicate with one another. "As a result, FEMA may be hindered in its ability to perform disaster response in an effective and timely manner," the report stated. The report by Department of Homeland Security Inspector General Richard Skinner was completed before this month’s storms flooded communities across the Midwest. In a detailed response, FEMA acknowledged the same shortcomings, said it had already begun upgrading its logistics systems, and claimed progress is on track for further improvements in the coming months and years. It remains unclear how the logistical gaps identified in the report may impact relief efforts for this month’s flooding—the agency’s largest challenge since Hurricanes Katrina and Rita devastated the Gulf Coast in 2005. Those disasters exposed deep flaws in FEMA’s ability to track food, water, ice, and other critical supplies, prompting Congress to restructure the agency so that its director now reports directly to the DHS secretary. FEMA operates eight permanent distribution centers across the U.S. and its territories, stocked with supplies and equipment. However, its logistics systems do not track disaster goods from initial shipment to final delivery, according to Skinner’s report. During emergencies, supplies are shipped from distribution centers to Federal Operational Staging Areas (FOSAs), then to state facilities or direct distribution points for victims. FEMA’s tracking system follows goods only as far as the FOSAs—not beyond. FEMA managers must regularly contact field staff during disasters, forcing them to spend valuable time manually tracking inventory. Field teams developed an unofficial "eFOSA" system to monitor inventory, but it does not run on FEMA’s secure network. The agency has contracted a vendor to upgrade its order-tracking system, but field personnel warn the new system will be slower and less user-friendly. The system also fails to account for goods shipped to FOSAs by other agencies, such as the Army Corps of Engineers. For example, it could not track cots provided by the American Red Cross during the 2007 California wildfires. Additionally, FEMA uses two separate systems to track commodities like food and water, versus property like generators and cell phones. "Without a comprehensive system, FEMA personnel must spend extra time and effort to manage goods," the report concluded. "For example, preparing a kit of furniture and supplies for a field office requires numerous manual steps."
