article_content: Mark Burns-Williamson, the elected Police and Crime Commissioner for West Yorkshire, has faced criticism for using a seven-year-old Audi A4 that was seized from a drug dealer under the Proceeds of Crime Act. Originally worth about £25,000, the vehicle is now shared among staff in his office as a cost-saving measure — avoiding rental fees and mileage claims. Local councillor Phil Scott argues the car’s association with criminal activity and its premium appearance send a troubling signal, particularly when many police stations are in disrepair and budgets are stretched thin. Scott and others urge the vehicle be sold, with proceeds reinvested into community policing. Burns-Williamson maintains the arrangement saves public money, noting that the car is not new and serves a functional purpose. However, critics question whether a commissioner earning £100,000 per year should be seen driving a vehicle once owned by a criminal, even if legally acquired. The car is officially owned by the police force, insured with public funds, and maintained using taxpayer resources. While the vehicle is modest by modern standards, its origins and visibility have ignited a debate over accountability, perception, and the symbolic weight of public asset use.

article_content: Ryan Taylor has returned to full training with Newcastle United after being sidelined for two years due to a persistent knee injury. The 29-year-old midfielder, who previously played for Wigan Athletic, suffered a cruciate ligament tear in 2012 and re-injured the same knee in April 2013 — forcing him to miss the entire 2013–14 season. Now back at the club’s High Benton training ground, Taylor shared his joy on Twitter: 'What a fantastic feeling it was to be back in training this morning with the team. Moments like that are worth so much to me and my family.' He also thanked Newcastle fans for their unwavering support during his recovery: 'Thank you for all your support throughout my rehab — it’s been much easier with the encouragement you’ve given me.' When Taylor suffered his second cruciate rupture, fears emerged that his professional career might be over. However, renowned knee specialist Dr. Richard Steadman — famed for helping legends like Alan Shearer and Owen Hargreaves recover from similar injuries — enabled Taylor to continue playing. Beyond his physical rehab, Taylor remained engaged with the club during his absence, assisting manager Alan Pardew by scouting opponents throughout last season.

article_content: On Thursday, a 32-foot dead gray whale drifted beneath Colman Dock, a busy ferry terminal in downtown Seattle, emitting a strong odor and prompting officials to reroute some passenger ferries. The whale, believed to have died several days earlier, had entered the area from open waters during its annual southward migration from Alaska to Baja California, Mexico. Washington State Ferries spokesperson Broch Bender confirmed that the carcass was towed away from the dock Thursday afternoon to a nearby secure location. Biologists from NOAA Fisheries Service plan to conduct a full autopsy to determine the cause of death. Michael Milstein, a NOAA spokesperson, noted that while the whale was significantly decomposed, valuable information could still be gathered. It remains unclear whether the whale died near the dock or drifted there after perishing elsewhere. Public reports of the foul smell began late Wednesday, though ferry operations were not disrupted. Gray whales typically spend summers feeding in Alaskan waters before migrating along the Pacific Coast each fall — a journey that places them close to urban shorelines like Seattle’s. This incident occurs near the end of that seasonal migration period.

article_content: Over 300 extraordinary pieces of Indian jewelry and jeweled objects — some dating back 500 years — are now on display at the Kremlin in Moscow in the landmark exhibition 'India: Jewels that Enchanted the World'. Housed in the historic Belfry and One-Pillar Hall, the collection includes rare royal treasures such as turban ornaments, rigid collar-necklaces, peacock brooches, and ceremonial headdresses, many of which have never been shown publicly before. Crafted by master artisans of the Mughal courts and later adapted by European jewelers, the pieces showcase exquisite use of gold, diamonds, rubies, emeralds, sapphires, and enamel. Highlights include a 16th-century pendant adorned with 103 carved emeralds, a gold water vessel that doubles as a tobacco bowl, and a 70-centimeter-long wedding headdress set with pearls and diamonds. Renowned houses like Cartier, Van Cleef & Arpels, and Chaumet drew deep inspiration from Indian color palettes and motifs, creating iconic 'Tutti Frutti' designs for Indian royalty — most notably Maharaja Bhupinder Singh of Patiala, one of Cartier’s most prominent patrons. The exhibition brings together artifacts loaned by over 30 institutions worldwide, including the British Museum and the Victoria and Albert Museum, under the curation of the State Museums of the Moscow Kremlin and the Indo-Russian Jewellery Foundation, led by Dr. Elena Gagarina and diamond expert Alex Popov. Running from 12 April to 27 July 2014, the exhibit not only celebrates the artistry of Indian jewelry but also reveals the rich cultural dialogue between South Asia and Europe during the 19th and early 20th centuries.

Ezifakwa kwiBelfry neOne-Pillar Hall, izinyanga zezithembiso zemfundo ezintsha, ezihlala ezimbili, izinyanga zeziphumo, nezimboni ezibiza, eziningi ezisayile ekukhulunywa. Iindlela ezifanayo ziyahlula: i-pendant ye-16th century eyodwa ezi103 emerodi ezikhuluma, i-gold water vessel enkulu eza kusebenzisa njengoba yilokhi, nase-70 cm uheaddress yomntwana wokuthandaza. Isifundazwe sisebenzisa izinyanga ezifakwa ngabanye abafunda abanani ezi30, njenge-British Museum ne-Victoria and Albert Museum, ngokucacisa kwiState Museums of the Moscow Kremlin ne-Indo-Russian Jewellery Foundation, ezibuyela kuDr. Elena Gagarina ne-alex Popov, umntwana ophakeme kakhulu kwezinyanga. Ukufakwa kuka-12 April ukuya ku-27 July 2014, isifundazwe sibonisa ukukhuluma kwezinyanga zaseIndia, nokukhuluma kwezinto ezingaphakathi kweSouth Asia neEurope kwi-19th ne-20th centuries.

article_content: In a heartbreaking family tragedy, 17-year-old Keandre Washington has been arrested and charged with killing his older brother, Bobby, 25, inside their Northwoods, Missouri home. According to authorities, Keandre allegedly attacked Bobby with a hammer early Tuesday morning, causing fatal head injuries. Their mother, terrified by what she witnessed, ran out of the house to seek help. Police arrived to find Bobby dead on the floor, with multiple blunt-force trauma wounds consistent with a hammer strike. Keandre is now facing charges of second-degree murder and armed criminal action, and remains in custody on $200,000 bail. Investigators say they still don’t know what sparked the violent confrontation. Meanwhile, this case has drawn renewed attention to a troubling trend in St. Louis: hammer-related homicides. Just last week, a group of teenagers was charged with killing Zemir Begic, a Bosnian immigrant, also using hammers — a crime some believe was racially motivated. With 148 murders recorded in the St. Louis region so far this year, Mayor Francis Slay is pushing for the creation of a dedicated gun court, saying, 'We should have no tolerance for violence in the city — we have way too many guns.' But this latest case raises questions beyond firearms: how do everyday objects become weapons in moments of rage, and what does it say about the emotional and social fractures within our communities?

article_content: More than two years after Facebook acquired Instagram, its influence on the parent platform is becoming clear. Facebook is now rolling out an automatic photo enhancement feature to its iOS app, suggesting edits before uploads — though users retain full control to adjust or remove them. A small wand icon in the corner indicates when an enhancement has been applied. Tapping it reverts the image to its original state. Manual adjustments are possible via a slider, while cropping and filtering remain accessible through the editor. This feature, previously optional, is launching first on iOS, with Android support to follow. The update coincides with Instagram’s introduction of five new filters: Slumber, Crema, Ludwig, Perpetua, and Aden — the first additions since December 2012, bringing the total to 25. Instagram explains these new filters are subtler, designed to complement modern smartphone cameras’ higher image quality rather than compensate for poor resolution. They aim to reflect the mood and tone of the moment with minimal editing. Alongside the filters, Instagram has added three new tools: slow-motion video uploads, real-time comment visibility (no refresh needed), and a perspective adjustment feature. Users can now also personalize their filter tray and view updated previews. Filter preferences vary globally: Amaro is the top choice in the UK, Germany, France, Russia, Japan, and Australia. In South Korea, Valencia reigns supreme. Other popular filters include Mayfair, X-Pro II, Lo-fi, Rise, and Hudson, depending on the region. Separately, Facebook’s AI lab head, Yann LeCun, revealed plans for a Digital Assistant that could use image recognition to identify potentially embarrassing photos — such as those taken while intoxicated — and prompt users to reconsider before posting. This feature is still under development.
translated_content: Kwakhona izinyanga ezimbili ngaphandle kuka-Facebook ephinda u-Instagram, ukuthi iyingcwele yayo kwi-platform enkulu iyathetha. U-Facebook uyaqhubeka umthombo wokuhlelwa kwamanzi esetyenziswayo kwi-iOS app, ukuze ibonise amathuba aphakathi kufika kwindawo — kodwa abaqhelwane bangasizwa ukuba bazokukhanya okanye kuzokubuyela. Isiqhingi sasezantseni siyabonisa ukuthi ukuhlelwa kusetyenziswa. Ukuxhuma kwindawo esikhundleni siphatha imiyalelo emuva kwesikhathi esilungileyo. Ukulandelana kufuneka kusebenzise isixhobo esinamandla, kodwa ukuphucula nokuhlala kufuneka kusetyenziswa kwindawo yokuhlelwa. Ukuze kubhekwa ukuthi kuyiphi indawo eyenza izinto zonke, kuyathetha kwi-iOS kwaye kuya kusetyenziswa kwi-Android. Ukuqhubeka kuyathetha nge-Instagram ephinda ephila amafitha amahlanu: Slumber, Crema, Ludwig, Perpetua, neAden — izinto eziningi ezinamagama emuva kwalo December 2012, kwaye kuyadala isiphumo esihlanzene nasezinye izinto eziningi 25. U-Instagram uqonde ukuthi amafitha angu-5 ayihleli ngokuchanekileyo, kuzo kuyisebenzisa umthetho olinganayo ngecamera ezinhle ezintsha kuba akukho ukukhuluma kwiimiyalelo eziningi. Bazokukhuluma ukuthi kufuneka uzifumene umoya, ububanzi, nezimo zomthetho ngokuphucula. Ngezinye izinto, u-Instagram uqhubeka izinto ezine-3: ukuphinda ukuphila amapicha aphakade, ukubona izinhliziyo ezithetha ngokushesha (akukho ukuthi ufikelele umthetho), kwaye ukubuyisela umoya wamanzi njengesixhobo sesetshenziswa. Abaqhelwane baza kufuneka bathole ukubuyisela isixhobo samafitha kwaye kuyadala imibhalo ephinda. Izimo zokusebenza zonke zifaniswa ngokubalulekileyo: Amaro yindawo engasekho kwi-UK, u-Germany, u-France, u-Russia, u-Japan, kwaye u-Australia. NgeKorea, Valencia yindawo engasekho. Izinto eziningi ezinamagama ezingcono ni-Mayfair, X-Pro II, Lo-fi, Rise, kwaye Hudson, ngokwesimo. Kwakugcina, u-Yann LeCun, umtshato wama-AI ka-Facebook, uwelisa ukuthi i-Digital Assistant ayazokwenza ukubona amapicha aphakade apho abaqhelwane baphendula — njengezithelo ezifakwe ngokushesha — kwaye uyazokukhonta abaqhelwane ukuba bazokuvula.

article_content: On 30 April 2013, a high-speed chase ended in a violent crash in Cleckheaton, West Yorkshire, leaving two police officers trapped in their unmarked BMW. The incident began when an Audi failed to stop for police in a marked patrol car in the nearby town of Scholes and fled toward Cleckheaton. At approximately 3:10 a.m., the Audi collided with the pursuing unmarked BMW police vehicle, sending both cars crashing into the wall of a building on Horncastle Street. The force of the impact scattered debris across the street, including the Audi’s engine. Two officers — a police officer and a Special Constable — were extracted from the wreckage and transported to Leeds General Infirmary with non-life-threatening injuries. The Audi’s driver, a 23-year-old man from Bradford, was found near the scene and taken to Pinderfields Hospital with serious but non-life-threatening injuries. His 25-year-old passenger was treated for a non-life-threatening chest injury at Bradford Royal Infirmary. Both men have been arrested in connection with the incident. The Independent Police Complaints Commission (IPCC) has launched an investigation into the circumstances, including whether the initial police vehicle was marked and whether a formal pursuit was underway. West Yorkshire Police declined to comment on these details while the probe continues.

Ukulungiswa kuyabeka ngenxa yezikholwa ezimnyama e-Scholes esikhundleni sasemfazeni, kwaye ezinyeni e-Cleckheaton. Bathini baphakamisa kakhulu. I-IPCC iyazalisa ukuthandaza ekutheni, njengoko ukuthi izikholwa ezimnyama ezimnye ziyahlukene kanye nesiphelo esinayo. article_content: It wasn’t your typical welcome-home banner. In Bremerton, Washington, the wife of a returning soldier displayed a sign above their front door that read: 'Welcome Home Cheater.' The image, captured by a local resident and later shared on Reddit by user Farthoven, quickly drew attention online. The town of Bremerton, home to a major Navy shipyard and Naval Hospital Bremerton on Puget Sound, has seen many service members return from deployment in recent weeks. The photograph was reportedly passed from a woman who showed it to a barista, who then sent it to Farthoven — making him a third-party recipient with no direct connection to the scene. While the full story behind the sign remains unclear, the image sparked both sympathy and mockery. One Reddit user sarcastically remarked: 'In other news, Daniel B. Cheater returned home today from Afghanistan to a warm reception from friends and family.' The post contrasts this public rebuke with the more common, heartfelt reunions typically seen when troops come home. The wife’s accusation of infidelity has not been independently verified.

article_content: Earlier this summer, Kelsey Mirkovic, a disease detective with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), entered a hut in Gueckedou, Guinea, with her team to speak with a man diagnosed with Ebola. Their goal: identify everyone he had contacted while infectious, to prevent further spread. 'Who lives with you? Who ate from the same plate? Who bathed or cared for you?' they asked. He named only his wife. But Mirkovic and her team knew this was inaccurate — they were aware he had children, and in West African communities, close family and neighbors often share meals and provide hands-on care for the sick. They explained that naming contacts would help protect lives — and that those listed would be treated with dignity. Still, he refused. This scenario repeated itself again and again. A CDC colleague working in Liberia noted preliminary data suggesting 40 to 60% of Ebola patient contacts remain unreported. 'This is one of the hardest parts of the response,' said Dr. Brett Petersen, a CDC medical officer. Mirkovic agrees. She understands why patients withhold names: rumors circulated that being placed on a contact list meant certain death — and that deaths occurred in the exact order listed. 'I understand they’re scared,' she said. 'But it’s very frustrating.' The Ebola outbreak in Guinea, Sierra Leone, Liberia, and Nigeria has claimed nearly 1,500 lives. A single untraced contact could spark a new chain of transmission. 'It’s like fighting a forest fire,' said CDC Director Dr. Thomas Frieden. 'If you leave behind even one burning ember, one undetected case, it could reignite the epidemic.' WHO Director-General Dr. Margaret Chan called contact tracing 'a formidable challenge,' noting that in some areas, transmission chains have gone underground — invisible and unreported. No precise figure exists for missing contacts, but Petersen estimated the 40–60% range based on averages: patients reported only two contacts, while households typically have five or six members. When patients were uncooperative, Mirkovic’s team turned to neighbors or community leaders for clues — sometimes successfully, sometimes not. 'Unfortunately, there’s nothing we can do,' she said. 'We can’t force them.' The WHO estimates that 10% of contacts will eventually develop symptoms. Some of these cases also go unreported: 'Many families hide infected loved ones at home,' according to a recent WHO statement. Mirkovic, who departed Guinea in late July, believes trust may grow as health workers build stronger community ties. But another obstacle remains: staffing shortages. In Sierra Leone alone, 2,000 contacts require monitoring, yet Doctors Without Borders reports having only followed up with about 200. Teams in Sierra Leone and Liberia are 'stretched to the breaking point' as the epidemic 'spirals out of control.'

Ukuze abonakele izikhathi zabo zemvula, 'Yini abantu abalwana nako? Yini ababiza ngokuphila? Yini abafuna ukuhamba nokulahla?' aba. Ake ngokukhawuleza. Baphendula ukuthi ukuvumela izikhathi ziyayithatha izinkinga zomthetho, kodwa abantu abaninzi abathandaza ukubuyela. Ngoko ke, abantu abaninzi abathandaza ukubuyela. 'Ngiyazifuna ukuthi bangakhetha ukuthi bakhuluma,' uMirkovic. 'Kodwa kungenxa yemva.' Izincwadi zomthetho eGuinea, Sierra Leone, Liberia neNigeria zihlala 1500. 'Abantu abaninzi abathandaza ukubuyela.' UDr. Mirkovic, ophakathi kwesikhathi esikhethele eGueckedou, uza kuthi: 'Kungasekho ukuthi siyafunda.' Kodwa kungenxa yemva: ukuthi kungasekho ukuthi siyafunda. Esidlengeni, 2000 izikhathi ziyayithatha, kodwa u-Doctors Without Borders uzithi ukuthi siyafunda nje 200. article_content: Earlier this week, Nigerian authorities uncovered 13 shipping containers at the Port of Lagos loaded with an arsenal of illegal weapons — including rockets, grenades, and ammunition. According to CMA CGM, the global logistics firm handling the shipment, the containers had been falsely labeled as carrying harmless goods like glass wool and stone pallets. The shipment originated from Bandar Abbas, a port in southern Iran, and arrived in Lagos in July. After being stored at a local depot, the consignee — identified by CMA CGM as an Iranian trader — requested to redirect the containers to Gambia, providing what appeared to be legitimate customs paperwork. However, Nigerian security forces stepped in before the move could happen. The discovery comes amid growing tensions ahead of Nigeria’s highly anticipated 2011 general elections, which experts warn could spark widespread unrest.

Ukuqala kweBandar Abbas, umphathi we-Iran, ukuqala eLagos kwesikhathi esidlule kwiJulayi. Ngaphambi kokuba kuziphindwe, umsebenzi wakho — othethwayo eCMA CGM njengomsebenzisi we-Iran — awazi ukuba ziyakusindwa eGambia, nokuthi azangezwe amandla okukhuluma. article_content: Labour leader Ed Miliband faced widespread criticism over the party’s opposition to military intervention in Syria, with UK Foreign Secretary William Hague stating that Labour’s stance had caused 'serious concern' among global leaders. Internally, Labour was deeply divided: some members, including former culture secretary Ben Bradshaw, warned that the party risked abandoning its internationalist values, while others, like Shadow Defence Secretary Jim Murphy, maintained that evidence-based military action could still be justified under strict conditions. International partners, particularly Washington and Paris, expressed strong disapproval. A Foreign Office source confirmed that the US and France were 'very unimpressed' with the UK’s position. Murphy acknowledged that Syrian President Bashar al-Assad had used chemical weapons and likely would again, but stressed that any intervention must meet legal criteria, including UN backing and compelling evidence. Meanwhile, Shadow Foreign Secretary Douglas Alexander argued that Prime Minister David Cameron must honor his public commitment not to participate in military action, warning that reversing course would damage public trust. Former Labour MP Meg Munn, one of the few to vote with the government, blamed both Miliband and Cameron for Britain’s confusing and indecisive posture. Miliband defended the party’s position, insisting it had not harmed the UK’s 'Special Relationship' with the US. In a candid moment, Murphy admitted to shouting profanities at Education Secretary Michael Gove after being accused of appeasing Assad, later apologizing for his 'industrial language' that 'his priest would not be proud of.'

Kwimeko, u-Labour uyaphakamiswa ngokucacile: abanye abakhuluma, njengenqanawa yezikholo yama-Labour Ben Bradshaw, bathi ukuthi umlilo wabantu akusazisa ukuthi abantu bakhuluma ngokuzihlakaniphisa, kodwa abanye, njenge-Jim Murphy, abhalela ukuthi umthombo omkhulu ukuze kuyisizathu esinokuthi sivunyelwe ngezinhlelo ezininzi. Abahlali abasekunene, kule mhlaba nase-Paris, bathi 'ukuthembeka' nge-ukuphila. Umphumela we-Foreign Office wayethetha ukuthi ama-Amerika ne-France bathi 'awukho kuzo.' U-Murphy wayethetha ukuthi u-Bashar al-Assad ubhekise izithombe zokugcina, kodwa uqinisekisa ukuthi ukuthengiselana kufanele kubaluleka, kuya ku-UN, nokuthi izithombe ziyakho. Kodwa, u-Douglas Alexander, umlenyaki we-Foreign, wayethetha ukuthi u-Cameron kufanele uqinisekise indlela yayo yobuso, ukuthi kungenzeka ukuthi ukwenzela izinkinga zokuphila. U-Meg Munn, umlenyaki we-Labour osebenza ngokuphila, wayebhekisa naye naye u-Cameron ngokuthi abathembekile ukuthi u-Britain akukho ukuthengiselana ngesikhathi esikhulu. U-Miliband wayethetha ukuthi i-stance yama-Labour ayayiphatha 'i-Special Relationship' nase-Amerika. Ngesikhathi esifundisayo, u-Murphy wayethetha ukuthi wayesilima 'i-industrial language' ku-Michael Gove njengoba wayethetha ukuthi u-Labour awukho ukuthengiselana, kodwa wayenokuthi 'ubaba wami awaqhubeka.'

article_content: ISLAMABAD, Pakistan (CNN) — Pakistani forces have reportedly killed up to 200 Taliban militants in the past 24 hours during operations in the Swat and Shangla regions, according to military officials. The military has intensified its campaign against the Taliban in the Swat Valley, now entering its third week. However, CNN cannot independently verify these claims, as journalists are currently barred from the area. The military accused Taliban fighters of causing civilian casualties through indiscriminate mortar attacks and the placement of improvised explosive devices (IEDs) along roads and in populated areas including Thana, Malakand, and Mingora. To allow civilians to escape the fighting, authorities have temporarily lifted the curfew, permitting movement between 6 a.m. and 3 p.m. local time (7 p.m. Saturday to 4 a.m. Sunday EDT). The United Nations refugee agency has warned of a 'massive displacement,' with an estimated 150,000 to 200,000 people already fleeing the conflict, according to UNHCR spokesperson Ron Redmond, citing provincial government data. An additional 300,000 are either on the move or expected to leave soon. On Sunday, two Pakistani soldiers were killed in action; a third died from wounds sustained on Friday. Despite repeated military announcements of battlefield successes, no verifiable evidence—such as photographs or body recoveries—has been presented to confirm the scale of Taliban losses. The lack of independent access raises questions about the true impact of the offensive. As fears mount that the Taliban could destabilize Pakistan—a nuclear-armed nation and key U.S. ally—the international community watches closely.

article_content: During the high-stakes India vs Australia World Cup final in Ahmedabad, an unexpected moment unfolded not on the pitch, but on social media. The BJP’s official X account cheered Team India with a simple, 'Come on Team India! We believe in you!' — a standard fan message. The Congress replied with 'TRUE THAT! JEETEGA INDIA.' At first glance, it looked like rare bipartisan solidarity. But savvy internet users quickly spotted the punchline: 'INDIA' wasn’t just a team name — it was the acronym for the opposition alliance, the Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance, launched earlier that year. The Congress was subtly nodding to their coalition’s branding, turning a sports cheer into a political wink. The BJP didn’t miss a beat. They doubled down on their long-standing preference for the term 'Bharat,' framing it as a reclaiming of India’s pre-colonial identity. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma took it further, updating his Twitter bio from 'India' to 'BHARAT,' and tweeting that the real battle isn't political — it’s civilizational. 'The British called it India,' he wrote. 'We fight for Bharat.' Meanwhile, fans flocking to Ahmedabad for the match faced skyrocketing hotel rates and flight costs, a reminder that big events come with big price tags. Unrelated stories about OpenAI’s leadership shakeup and government IT subsidies were published alongside but did not connect to the cultural moment. The real story? A cricket final that briefly turned politics into wordplay.

article_content: Scores of firefighters from two counties converged on the Yorkshire Moors to battle widespread fires that blazed through the night. More than 40 firefighters from Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service joined crews from West Yorkshire to tackle pockets of fire stretching from Mytholmroyd in Yorkshire to Littleborough in Rochdale. At least 14 fire engines were dispatched to the scene, where one blaze reached over a mile in length, threatening isolated cottages and farmhouses. The dry ground remained smoldering the following day after crews worked through the night to contain the flames. Throughout the night, firefighters maintained a presence on the moors to safeguard remote properties, resuming active firefighting at first light. The fires had spread across dry vegetation from West Yorkshire into neighboring areas. Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service reported that six fire engines and an operational support unit responded to a fire behind the Summit pub on Todmorden Road at approximately 7:30 p.m. Additional engines from Rochdale and Littleborough joined six Yorkshire-based units in combating scattered fires across the moorland. After hours of battling the flames, crews temporarily withdrew from the hillside for safety as darkness fell. Firefighters used strategically positioned fire engines to shield vulnerable properties, continuously monitoring for flare-ups. A ranger used a power hose to prevent further spread of flames on the smoldering moorland. Strong winds and dry conditions enabled fires to spread rapidly. Crews from Manchester and Pontefract supported local teams near Baitings Reservoir. Station Manager Pete Buckley said: 'Overnight, we protected remote properties with water sprays, monitored fire spread, and tracked wind shifts. At its peak, we had eight fire engines and an operational support unit engaged. First light gives us the best conditions to resume offensive operations and continue defending vulnerable structures.' West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service noted that crews used beaters, backpack pumps, ultra-lightweight water systems, and water shuttles to fight the blaze. Firefighters from Mytholmroyd, Todmorden, Halifax, Huddersfield, Mirfield, and Skelthorpe responded, alongside specially trained wildfire officers. The cause of the fires remains under investigation by both services. Additional pockets of fire erupted near Baitings Reservoir, close to the M62 motorway, on the previous evening. Specialist wildfire crews were among the dozens of responders who operated through the night.

article_content: By Reuters. Published: 13:35 EST, 7 March 2014 | Updated: 14:00 EST, 7 March 2014. The Supreme Court of Canada ruled on Friday that a man from Nova Scotia, Craig Jaret Hutchinson, is guilty of sexual assault for deliberately puncturing condoms during consensual sex with his girlfriend in an attempt to impregnate her. His girlfriend, whose identity the court has protected, stated she agreed to sex only if condoms were used to prevent pregnancy. In a unanimous 7-0 decision, the court held that while she consented to sex, she did not consent to unprotected sex — and that tampering with the condoms constituted fraud, thereby invalidating legal consent. Chief Justice Beverley McLachlin and Justice Thomas Cromwell, joined by two other justices, wrote: 'We conclude that there was no consent in this case by reason of fraud... Mr. Hutchinson is therefore guilty of sexual assault.' The other three judges reached the same conclusion through a different legal reasoning path. According to the prosecution’s statement of facts, Hutchinson sought to get his girlfriend pregnant in 2006 to salvage their deteriorating relationship. Although her pregnancy temporarily extended the relationship, she later had an abortion and ended things with him. After the breakup, Hutchinson sent his ex-partner a text message saying, 'I wanted a baby with you so bad.' Although the court could not definitively establish that the pregnancy resulted from the tampered condoms, Hutchinson’s intent and deceptive act were sufficient for conviction. Hutchinson, who had been released on bail, must now serve an 18-month prison sentence. This case echoes the landmark 1992 ruling against Henry Cuerrier of British Columbia, who was convicted of sexual assault for having unprotected sex with two women without disclosing his HIV status — even though neither contracted the virus. The court determined that nondisclosure amounted to fraud. Similarly, Hutchinson’s actions were deemed fraudulent and criminal.

article_content: By Mike Dawes. Phil Mickelson, Rory McIlroy, Justin Rose, Luke Donald, Lee Westwood, Rickie Fowler, and some of the world’s best golfers competed in a flop shot challenge filmed during the 2014 Scottish Open in Aberdeen. The European Tour challenged the players to hit shots over a cardboard cutout of Phil Mickelson — a safety precaution after previous challenges used live people. Mickelson, who had already been practicing flop shots throughout the week, started the tournament with a backward flop shot that led to a birdie. Louis Oosthuizen cleared the cutout easily but didn’t finish among the top three closest to the pin. Thomas Bjorn won the challenge by landing his shot just 5cm from the pin, after it bounced around the hole. Luke Donald came second at 21cm, and Mickelson himself placed third at 39cm. Other players showed off playful antics: Russell Knox nearly knocked the cutout’s head off, Lee Westwood tried to shoot between its legs, and Miguel Ángel Jiménez executed a backheel kick over it.

article_content: For ten hours, Shoshana B. Roberts walked through the bustling streets of New York City, microphones in hand, while filmmaker Rob Bliss recorded from behind in a backpack-mounted camera. What followed wasn’t just noise — it was a relentless stream of unsolicited comments: 'God bless you, mami,' 'Hey baby,' 'You don’t wanna talk?' — each one a reminder of how everyday public spaces can become hostile for women, LGBTQ individuals, and people of color. The raw footage became a powerful 1 minute 56 second public service announcement produced in partnership with Hollaback!, an organization dedicated to ending street harassment. Inspired by his girlfriend’s own encounters, Bliss aimed to expose how normalized this behavior has become. Hollaback! emphasizes that while such interactions may seem minor, they’re part of a broader pattern that hits women, LGBTQ people, people of color, and young individuals hardest — often escalating into intimidation or physical danger. Within hours of the video going viral on YouTube, the comments section filled with threats, forcing Hollaback! to enlist help moderating abuse. The campaign doesn’t just document harassment — it challenges society to stop treating it as harmless banter, and to recognize it as a form of control rooted in systemic inequality.

article_content: Six months after being released from jail following a 13-year clerical error, Cornealious 'Mike' Anderson, 37, was arrested again—this time on charges of second-degree robbery in St. Louis. Anderson had spent more than a decade living as a free man after a 2000 conviction for armed robbery of a Burger King employee went unenforced due to a paperwork failure. He built a life: marrying his wife LaQonna, raising four children, starting a carpentry business, coaching youth football, and volunteering at church. In May 2023, Judge Terry Lynn Brown ruled Anderson had effectively served his full 13-year sentence and ordered his release, calling him 'a changed man' and praising his rehabilitation. But early Sunday morning, Anderson was taken into custody after a woman reported being robbed at gunpoint—her purse snatched from her shoulder and briefly dragged along the street. She identified him both at the scene and during a formal police lineup. His attorney, Patrick Megaro, strongly disputes the arrest, arguing Anderson’s clothing—a leather jacket, slacks, and light brown boots—did not match the suspect description (hoodie and Nike sneakers). He also insists Anderson was at a birthday party with over 40 witnesses that night. Prosecutor Jennifer Joyce maintains the victim’s identification is reliable and notes the victim never described the suspect as wearing Nikes or a hoodie, but rather a leather jacket and boots—consistent with what Anderson was wearing. Anderson remains free on $10,000 bond. His family and lawyer believe his history made him an easy target for law enforcement, despite the lack of evidence linking him to the crime. 'He has everything to lose,' Megaro said. 'Why would he risk his family, his job, his freedom—for a purse?' The case has reignited debate about how the justice system treats those who rebuild their lives after mistakes—and whether past records unfairly overshadow present innocence.

article_content: Over £250,000 has been paid to four civil servants accused of serious misconduct—including harassment, breaching safety regulations, and failing to complete assigned tasks—according to a report by the National Audit Office (NAO). The NAO uncovered 95 controversial severance agreements across five government departments, totaling £3.4 million. Of these, 84 included confidentiality clauses, and 74 contained provisions that prevented employees from reporting issues to oversight bodies such as the Care Quality Commission or the Department of Health. The Department for Culture, Media and Sport faced particular scrutiny, approving four payments linked to alleged failures: one employee was suspended over harassment claims, while others were paid for not meeting performance standards or violating workplace conduct rules. In one case, a manager who raised alarms about fraud and patient safety was dismissed, only to be reinstated after an employment tribunal. By then, their position had been made redundant, and they received a severance package with a confidentiality agreement. The Treasury approved these payments despite guidance stating that severance should never reward failure, dishonesty, or inappropriate behavior. Legal advice frequently cited the risk of losing unfair dismissal cases as justification—even when misconduct was substantiated but due process was flawed. The Ministry of Defence and Department of Health were also criticized for approving payouts after failing to follow internal employment procedures. In one instance, a contractor nurse received compensation because official hiring guidelines were ignored. The NAO has called for clearer government guidance on compromise agreements and demands public disclosure of settlement data to identify departments with unusually high rates of such deals.

article_content: Cinemark set a record in revenue during the third quarter, thanks to blockbusters including Barbie and Oppenheimer, and even surpassed pre-pandemic 2019 levels by 6%. The major exhibitor reported revenue of $875 million for the quarter ending September 30, a 35% increase compared to the same period last year. Diluted earnings per share of 61 cents marked a return to profitability, reversing last year’s loss of 20 cents per share. July was Cinemark’s highest-grossing domestic box office month ever, driven by the cultural phenomenon of Barbie and Oppenheimer. Songs of Freedom, an unexpected hit, also provided a welcome boost for theater owners. However, the current fourth quarter may pose challenges, as the ongoing SAG-AFTRA strike has delayed several upcoming film releases. Total admissions across the U.S. and Latin America reached 62 million. Cinemark noted it is the only major U.S. exhibitor to achieve a meaningful increase in market share since the pandemic. Net debt decreased to $2.4 billion from $2.5 billion a year ago. Headquartered in Plano, Texas, Cinemark has remained less debt-encumbered than its competitors during years of operational strain. 'As we assess the fundamental drivers of our industry’s and company’s long-term health and prosperity — particularly consumer behavior trends, key indicators for new release volume recovery over time, and the significant range of incremental revenue and productivity opportunities fully within our control — we remain highly optimistic about the future,' said CEO Sean Gamble in the earnings release.

article_content: A NEW OIL REALITY: After more than three years of high oil prices, oil-exporting regions enjoyed a significant economic boom. However, new data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) suggests this era may be shifting. The EIA projects that U.S. oil imports will decline while domestic crude production continues to rise. If realized, this surge in American output could put downward pressure on global crude prices — potentially forcing oil-dependent economies to rethink their energy strategies. In a conversation with Marketplace Middle East (MME), Tony Hayward — former CEO of BP and current CEO of Genel Energy — shares insights on the evolving energy landscape. He discusses the growth of oil operations in Iraq and reflects on lessons learned during his tenure at BP. article_content: Sanaa, Yemen (CNN) — The deputy leader of al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula and one of Saudi Arabia’s most wanted fugitives has been declared dead by a prominent jihadist, though Yemeni officials say they have no evidence confirming his death. Abu Sufyan al-Azdi, also known as Saeed al-Shahri, died 'after a long journey in fighting the Zio-Crusader campaign,' according to a tweet by jihadist Abdulla bin Muhammad, as reported by SITE Intelligence Group, which monitors global terrorism. It remains unclear how al-Azdi died. SITE cited media reports suggesting he succumbed to injuries from a December drone strike. The Arabic news network Al-Arabiya also reported his death, citing family sources. However, three senior Yemeni Defense Ministry officials told CNN they have no proof of his death. 'We have no evidence to confirm his death, and our government continues to pursue the leadership of the terrorist network,' one official said on condition of anonymity, as he is not authorized to speak to the media. More than 80 suspected al-Qaeda militants have been killed since early December, the official added, but al-Azdi is still believed to be at large. Al-Azdi has been reported dead before — most recently in September, when Yemen claimed he was killed in an air raid. A voice message released the following month appeared to feature al-Azdi asserting he was still alive. A Saudi national, al-Azdi spent six years in the U.S. military prison at Guantanamo Bay before being released in 2007. He fled to Yemen in 2008. U.S. drone activity targeting senior AQAP figures intensified in 2012. On Monday, a U.S.-led drone strike in Marib, an oil-rich province east of Yemen’s capital, killed two militants — identified by the defense ministry as Ali Saleh Toaiman and Qassim Nasser Toaiman — and wounded five others. On Saturday, two U.S. drone strikes in Marib and al-Baitha killed eight people. In October, Yemeni President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi announced an escalation in military cooperation with the United States against al-Qaeda. In response, AQAP launched multiple attacks on military and security personnel, killing more than 60 people, according to Yemen’s Interior Ministry.

Abu Sufyan al-Azdi, othi kakhulu Saeed al-Shahri, awafika 'ngokukhuluma ngezinyathelo ezinamandla ezingenisa i-Zio-Crusader campaign,' njengokuthi kuthetha Abdulla bin Muhammad, njengokuthi kubonakalwa ngu-SITE Intelligence Group, osayizi ukubona imithombo yezikhaliso ezingxenye. Ukuthi kanjani al-Azdi awafika akukho ukwazi. SITE ikhula izindaba zokuthi awafika ngokwesimo esingaphambili kwisikhathi se-drone emhlabeni Decemba. Isihloko sesizwe sa-Arabia Al-Arabiya sithi kuthi abafika, uzokuthi abafundisi. Kodwa abaphantsi abathathu abakholi kwe-Ministry of Defence be-Yemen bathi ku-CNN abangeke bangazange ukwazi. 'Singakwazi ukwazi ukuthi awafika, kodwa umlomo wethu uyathola izinkulungwane ze-terrorist network,' kuthi umntu ongabheka kakhulu ngokuthi akukho ukuvakela kwindaba. Izinto eziningi kuma-80 abasebenzi abakhawulezayo be-al-Qaeda bawafika emhlabeni Decemba, kuthi umntu, kodwa al-Azdi akakhulu kakhulu. Al-Azdi abonakalwa abafika phambi — ukuqala kwi-September, ukuze Yemen ithi awafika ngokwesimo esingaphambili. Isiphumo esikhulu esibonakalayo emhlabeni ophambili ukuze al-Azdi athi ukuthi awunakho. Umuntu we-Saudiya, al-Azdi ashintshelwa ngobushushu be-60 ku-Guantanamo Bay ukuze awukhale emhlabeni 2007. Awukhale e-Saudiya kuya e-Yemen emhlabeni 2008. I-Saturday, izikhathi ezimbini ze-drone e-U.S. abafika abaninzi abaninzi e-Marib nokho e-al-Baitha. Emhlabeni October, u-President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi wayethi ukuthi u-Yemen uyakwakha amandla awo e-U.S. ekupheleni kwe-al-Qaeda. article_content: Just hours after taking his first independent steps up the stairs, two-year-old JJ Michalowski was left permanently paralyzed from the chest down following a devastating car crash. The collision occurred on March 8 on the A628 bypass in Hemsworth, West Yorkshire, when Daniel Thrower, 34, lost control of a stolen Ford Mondeo and slammed into the family’s Peugeot 407. Thrower, who admitted to dangerous driving and aggravated vehicle taking, will be sentenced in September. JJ’s father and two sisters were also injured in the crash. His mother, Katy, recalls how proud she was that morning — JJ had just mastered walking up and down stairs like a grown-up. Now, she says, he can’t sit up alone and relies entirely on caregivers. Despite this, JJ smiles constantly, even through pain. Doctors initially feared brain damage, but an MRI revealed catastrophic spinal trauma. Remarkably, JJ has regained some use of his arms during rehabilitation — a sign of his fierce spirit. His family now seeks donations to buy him a custom joystick-controlled electric wheelchair so he can move independently. Meanwhile, Thrower, who requires a ventilator to sleep, faces almost certain jail time. The family’s Facebook page, 'Help Bring JJ Home,' is where people can contribute.

article_content: A ubiquitous Olive Garden TV commercial depicts a picturesque cooking school in Italy, as a voiceover uses terms like 'artisanal' and 'fonduta,' while smiling chefs in crisp white coats taste tomato sauce straight from a simmering pot and kiss their fingertips with delight. TV viewers turned to social media platforms such as Twitter and Facebook to question the chain's claim of 'culinary inspiration' from Tuscany: Is the so-called Culinary Institute of Tuscany a legitimate institution—or merely an advertising fabrication? Yes, Virginia, there is an Olive Garden Culinary Institute of Tuscany—though its ownership is shared. Each winter, approximately 100 top-performing U.S. Olive Garden chefs and managers attend an 11-week immersive program there, which began in 1999. For the rest of the year, the property—named Riserva di Fizzano—functions as a bed-and-breakfast, featuring the Rocca delle Macie winery, a guest house, a swimming pool, and a restaurant, according to Mark Jaronski, Director of Media and Communications at Darden Restaurants. Olive Garden is part of the Orlando-based Darden Restaurants family, which includes Red Lobster, LongHorn Steakhouse, The Capital Grille, Bahama Breeze, and Seasons 52. Chef Romana Neri, an executive chef based in Tuscany, leads the school. She supports Darden’s Executive Chef Paolo Lafata during his stays at the Tuscan campus. Culinary pilgrimages to study foreign cuisines are common among chefs: Julia Child trained in France, and Rick Bayless in Mexico. Skepticism arises when a chain restaurant claims authenticity. Menu items inspired by the institute are marked with the official 'Culinary Institute of Tuscany' seal—including Chianti Braised Short Ribs, Grilled Shrimp Caprese, and Smoked Mozzarella Fonduta. The public can also participate in a one-week Tuscan cooking experience—if they win Olive Garden’s annual sweepstakes. Judith Wilson of Spanish Fork, Utah—who lives 40 minutes from the nearest Olive Garden—was a 2009 winner. 'The cooking school welcomed us,' Wilson said. 'Every day, we learned about different olive oils, cheeses, wines, and how to pair them with meals.' During off-seasons, the Riserva di Fizzano’s restaurant, Relais-Agriturismo, serves authentic Tuscan dishes to guests. The estate also hosts public cooking classes to teach visitors about regional cuisine. Despite skepticism, Olive Garden continues to thrive: Darden Restaurants reported in March that U.S. same-restaurant sales rose 1.5% in its fiscal third quarter.

article_content: A teenager has been accused of murdering a 63-year-old man in a brutal, premeditated attack — then filming the crime scene to intimidate others, a court has heard. Bleddyn King, 18, allegedly stabbed David Evans 72 times inside his home in Pentyrch, near Cardiff, leaving the knife bent from the force. After the killing, King recorded a video of Evans’ body, delivering chilling threats: 'F*** around with me and this is what happens. You **** with me and you **** with the best.' According to prosecutors, King used a gay dating website under the alias 'Big Wolf 1993' to contact Evans, targeting him because he believed a gay man would be less likely to report a violent crime. David Evans, a retired father of two and widower, was described as a quiet, gentle man who had cared for his late wife during her illness. He lived alone after returning to Wales from France. King also killed Evans’ cat, Jess, before setting fire to the bungalow and fleeing. Prosecutors say the entire act was a coldly planned robbery, escalated by extreme violence and post-crime theatrics designed to instill fear. King denies charges of murder but has admitted to manslaughter. His trial continues at Cardiff Crown Court.

article_content: Morne van Wyk smashed an unbeaten 114 off just 70 balls — including nine fours and seven sixes — to guide South Africa to a commanding 195/3 in 20 overs against West Indies in Durban. His blistering knock helped the Proteas secure a decisive 69-run win in the third T20I, preventing a series whitewash. Reeze Hendricks (42) and David Wiese (21) provided crucial support in the innings, while Wiese later turned the tide with a devastating spell of 5/23 in four overs, dismantling the West Indies chase. West Indies, who won the toss and chose to field, struggled to break through early, allowing South Africa to reach 100 before losing their first wicket in the 13th over. After a promising start to their reply — with Dwayne Smith top-scoring on 5 — the visitors lost wickets at regular intervals, collapsing from 68/3 to 126/9. Key dismissals included Lendl Simmons (49), Andre Russell (12), and Darren Sammy (8), all falling to Wiese and other bowlers. With 70 needed off 18 balls, the task became impossible as Carlos Brathwaite (1) and Ashley Nurse (11) were removed in quick succession. Sheldon Cottrell was clean bowled for a golden duck on the penultimate ball, sealing the win for South Africa. Although defeated in this match, West Indies clinched the T20I series 2-1. The teams now turn their focus to a five-match ODI series, beginning Friday at the same venue.

article_content: In most cities, public transit brings together all kinds of people — but in Seattle, one four-legged passenger has stolen the hearts of commuters. Meet Eclipse, a black Labrador-bull mastiff mix who rides the bus alone every day to get to the dog park. She doesn’t need a leash or a ticket — just a clear sense of where she’s going. It all started when her owner, Jeff Young, stepped off the bus to smoke a cigarette and missed the departure. Eclipse, seemingly understanding the situation, hopped aboard by herself. Young boarded the next bus and found her waiting at their usual stop four stops later. Since then, it’s become a daily ritual. Bus drivers recognize her instantly. Passengers smile when they see her trotting down the aisle, sometimes even settling into a window seat to watch the neighborhood pass by. Local radio host Miles Montgomery was stunned when he spotted her looking out the window, clearly waiting for her stop. 'Did that just happen?' he asked. For Young, it’s no surprise. 'She’s been doing this for two years — she’s as urban as they come,' he says. Eclipse isn’t just a pet; she’s a beloved part of Seattle’s transit culture.

article_content: Nancy Lane, a 68-year-old retired NHS nurse from Aberdare, South Wales, died of acute liver failure three months after undergoing heart surgery at Morriston Hospital in Swansea. An inquest revealed she contracted Hepatitis B from a contaminated transoesophageal echocardiogram (TOE) probe—commonly called a 'magic eye'—that had not been properly sterilized between patients. At the time of her procedure in March 2011, there were no national guidelines governing the decontamination of these probes. Although the device was covered with a protective sheath during use and wiped with disinfectant afterward, the cleaning process was insufficient to eliminate the virus. Coroner Louise Hunt delivered a narrative verdict, concluding that Mrs. Lane’s death resulted directly from failures in infection control. The Abertawe Bro Morgannwg University Health Board apologized unreservedly and commissioned an independent review that led to 32 recommendations for improvement. Despite these changes, Mrs. Lane’s family reported that in August 2011—two months after her death—inspectors found visibly contaminated equipment, including items stained with blood, still in use. They argue that deeper systemic issues remain unresolved, particularly around staff training and institutional culture surrounding hygiene. Her family, devastated by her loss, say Nancy had devoted over 30 years to the NHS and trusted its caregivers implicitly. They now urge the Welsh Government to launch a public inquiry into infection control practices across NHS hospitals, calling for mandatory reviews every 12 months to ensure lasting change.

West Midlands Police have arrested two women in connection with the case: a 30-year-old believed to be the child’s mother, and a 50-year-old thought to be her grandmother. Both are currently assisting with police inquiries into possible neglect. A post-mortem examination is scheduled to establish the precise cause of death. The West Midlands Ambulance Service confirmed that their team acted swiftly and professionally under extremely difficult circumstances.

article_content: As jury selection moves forward in the high-profile case of James Holmes — accused of killing 12 and injuring 70 during a 2012 movie theater massacre in Aurora, Colorado — his court-appointed legal team has declined to disclose how much the defense is costing taxpayers. The Office of the State Public Defender, responsible for representing Holmes due to his inability to hire private counsel, insists that releasing financial details would violate attorney-client confidentiality and could unfairly aid prosecutors. They also claim they’re legally exempt from state open-records laws, a position supported by national experts who note that public defenders rarely break down costs per case, especially when managing over 160,000 cases annually on an $83 million budget. While estimates vary, media outlets suggest the entire trial could exceed $5.5 million — with Fox News placing the figure closer to $7 million. That total includes nearly $3 million in federal assistance allocated to victims and survivors to help them participate in the legal process. Additional expenses include over $460,000 spent on heightened security and $90,000 for closed-circuit television systems to accommodate victims unable to enter the small courtroom. The district attorney’s office alone has earmarked more than $775,000 for non-salary costs tied to the case, largely because prosecutors are pushing for the death penalty, a move the defense says unnecessarily drags out proceedings. District Attorney George Brauchler has publicly stated his intent to seek execution for Holmes, calling it ‘justice.’ But studies from the Death Penalty Information Center and Forbes indicate that death penalty trials cost roughly $1 million more than those seeking life without parole — and in states like California, the annual cost of executions can reach $137 million compared to just $11.5 million for life imprisonment. Despite mounting pressure from lawmakers like State Representative Polly Lawrence, who argues that taxpayers deserve to know how their money is spent, a proposed Colorado bill mandating cost disclosures was recently tabled in committee. Legal transparency advocate Steven Zansberg, who represents news organizations including the Associated Press, contends that public funding demands public accountability. ‘The people of this state have a right to know how much tax money is being expended, and how,’ he said. Yet public defender Doug Wilson countered that only 25 media requests had been made — all focused narrowly on Holmes — and that broader disclosure could compromise future cases. With salaries for lead defense attorneys at $165,756 and the DA earning $156,000, the debate isn't just about money — it’s about the balance between justice, secrecy, and the public’s right to oversight.

article_content: A Melbourne man has sparked concern after offering women money for sex through the dating app OKCupid. Daniel, 28, contacted several women asking if they had 'ever been offered money'—then named specific amounts and urged them to consider his proposal. None of the women reported the messages to police, as offering money for sex is not illegal in Australia, according to The Age. On his profile, Daniel described himself as being from Melbourne and 'extremely unlucky in love and not your average guy.' He used the account names dja86dj and daniel86dja, both of which he has since deleted. In his proposals to women based in Melbourne, Daniel initially offered $500, later increasing the amount to $1,000 and then $2,000. article_content: Napoli’s hopes of closing in on Serie A leaders AC Milan took a serious blow after a disappointing 2-0 away defeat to Chievo Verona. The result leaves Walter Mazzarri’s side six points behind the Rossoneri, despite Lazio holding Milan to a 0-0 draw the night before. Chievo struck early when striker Davide Moscardelli curled a precise left-footed shot off the post in the 20th minute. Just after the break, defender Gennaro Sardo sealed the win with a brilliant solo run, beating three defenders before slotting home. It was Chievo’s second victory over Napoli this season, following a 3-1 win in September. Meanwhile, other top sides also stumbled: Roma were held to a 1-1 draw at home by Brescia, with Marco Borriello scoring for Roma before Eder equalized. Juventus, under intense pressure, fell 2-1 to Palermo — a result that sees the Sicilian side leapfrog them into sixth. Fabrizio Miccoli opened the scoring with a stunning low finish past Gianluigi Buffon, and Giulio Migliaccio added another before Claudio Marchisio pulled one back. Juventus now have just three wins in eight league games this season under Luigi Delneri. Elsewhere, Udinese drew 1-1 with Bologna after trailing, Cagliari edged Sampdoria 1-0, Fiorentina beat Genoa 1-0, Cesena and Catania shared goals in a 1-1 stalemate, and Lecce climbed out of the relegation zone with a narrow 1-0 win at Parma. Inter Milan still have two games in hand and can overtake Lazio if they beat Bari on Thursday.

article_content: A 62-year-old skydiver, Mark Elizondo, is being treated for burns after landing on power lines during a parachute jump near Sacramento. He was airlifted to hospital over the weekend after the incident, which occurred around 2 p.m. on Sunday. Friends describe Elizondo as an experienced skydiver who had completed several jumps that day before the accident. His wife, Raedell, said he had been practicing a routine with 14 other skydivers when the accident happened. Elizondo, who met his wife while skydiving, has made more than 1,000 parachute jumps in his lifetime. Bill Dause, owner of the Lodi Parachute Center, called the incident 'a freak thing,' noting Elizondo had jumped there before. Dause told KCRA: 'For some reason, he just went too far downwind, and unfortunately, the power line was below him when he turned around to try to return.' Witnesses said Elizondo was conscious but burned and in shock when emergency responders arrived. Lieutenant Michael van Grouw confirmed Elizondo was alert and talking as he was transported on a stretcher. While Dause downplayed wind as a factor, other skydivers, like Ed Barr, argued that wind conditions worsened the risk and that control lies with the jumper. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is investigating the incident and will inspect the parachute’s condition and packing. FAA records show the Lodi Parachute Center received citations in 2010 and 2011 for failing to maintain aircraft equipment. Last year, an independent instructor at the center faced potential FAA penalties for improperly securing a harness during a tandem jump. In a separate incident, 80-year-old skydiver Laverne Everett slipped from her harness during a jump but landed safely and declined to criticize her instructor. Elizondo remains hospitalized for burn treatment. Fellow skydiver Bill Stanley remarked: 'Any sport has risks. People get killed in every sport that exists. Honestly, my drive out here is more frightening.' Dause added that he could recall only one other power-line incident since opening his business.

article_content: Only 19% of voters view Ed Miliband as a viable future Prime Minister, marking another setback for the Labour Party. A YouGov poll for The Times reveals that just 26% of the public believes Labour is ready to govern, while fewer than half of Labour’s own supporters (49%) think Miliband will become the country’s next leader. Former minister David Lammy warned that Labour has become overly focused on living standards, failing to articulate a compelling, positive alternative for voters. Major donor John Mills echoed concerns, stating Labour’s economic strategy now closely mirrors that of the Conservatives, leaving the party 'boxed in'. Miliband’s leadership has come under scrutiny following his muted response to the recent Budget, which many interpreted as a missed opportunity and a tactical win for the Tories. Recent weekend polls suggest Labour and the Conservatives are now effectively tied in voter support. Lammy cautioned that with 14 months until the next general election, Labour risks being drawn into a debate defined by Conservative priorities — deficit reduction, welfare, and immigration. 'We knock on doors and the central message is about living standards and energy prices,' Lammy told BBC Radio 4. 'But the electorate needs more than that. We must not let the election become a referendum on the government’s weakest points.' Labour Deputy Leader Harriet Harman countered that the party is making steady progress, acknowledging the challenge but insisting they are addressing the issues voters care about most.

article_content: In a shift that surprised many, the UK has climbed above Brazil to reclaim the sixth spot in the world’s largest economies — a position it lost exactly one year earlier. According to the Centre for Economics and Business Research (Cebr), the British economy is now on track to surpass France’s within the next couple of years, possibly as early as 2013 or 2014. However, this upward momentum won’t last forever. By the end of the decade, both India and Russia are projected to pull ahead of the UK, while Brazil is expected to bounce back and retake its former rank by 2014. Meanwhile, China continues its rapid ascent, currently at 53% the size of the US economy but forecasted to hit 83% by 2022. The US will remain number one, and Japan will hold onto third place, but Germany could lose its fourth spot to India’s explosive growth. India itself is set to become the largest economy in the Commonwealth by 2017, a development Cebr’s CEO Douglas McWilliams humorously noted: 'They beat us at cricket this winter — but they’re winning at economics.' France’s slowdown is largely attributed to President François Hollande’s 75% tax rate on top earners and ongoing eurozone challenges. Just a year ago, French Foreign Minister François Baroin confidently claimed that economically, 'we prefer being French than British.' Now, Cebr’s numbers suggest the opposite — though some analysts warn the UK may still lose its coveted AAA credit rating if it fails to reduce its debt burden by 2015. Italy faces a steeper fall, dropping from eighth to thirteenth globally, overtaken by nations like Turkey and Mexico. Meanwhile, Indonesia — home to over 238 million people — is expected to rocket from 16th to 10th, making it one of the most dramatic upward movements in global economic rankings.

Ngokuchanekileyo, i-Ekonomi yeBritani iyakusiza ukuthola indawo engu-6 ngenxa yezinhlelo zokuhlanganisa ezinikezwe nguCebr, kodwa izinto eziningi zazikhetha ukuba iziqhamo zizobuyela. Ngaphandle kwezinye izandla, i-India ne-Russia zizokhuluma kule ndawo ngezinye izandla, kodwa i-Brazil zizobuyela kwindawo yayo ngonyaka ka-2014. Kodwa i-China ibuyele kakhulu, ngaphandle kwezinye izandla, 53% yezinhlelo zika-US, kodwa izandla zizokubonakala kakhulu kakhulu ngokushesha kakhulu ngonyaka ka-2022. I-US izokhuluma kwindawo yokugcina, noma i-Japan izokhuluma kwindawo yokunye, kodwa i-Germany izokhuluma kwindawo yokunye kanye ne-India, okungabizwa ngokushesha kakhulu. Kodwa i-Indonesia — eya kwi-238 milyon — izokhuluma kwindawo yokunye kanye, ukuze abuye kwindawo yokunye kanye, okungabizwa ngokushesha kakhulu kwezinhlelo zemigomo ezingaphandle.

article_content: Morton Salt’s historic Chicago warehouse, famous for its giant rooftop sign reading 'When It Rains, It Pours,' experienced a dramatic incident on Tuesday when a side wall collapsed at approximately 2 p.m. The collapse sent massive amounts of white salt cascading onto the street, burying at least six vehicles parked nearby — including several at the adjacent McGrath Acura dealership, where at least three cars were completely engulfed, leaving only their front ends visible. No injuries were reported, according to Chicago Fire Department spokesman Larry Langford. City engineers are now assessing the structural integrity of the facility, a major storage site for Morton Salt, a 100-year-old company best known for its pourable table salt. The Chicago Police Department responded to the scene shortly after the collapse and closed Elston Avenue in both directions. They later shared photos on Twitter, prompting widespread online reaction. Many social media users pointed out the eerie appropriateness of the company’s iconic slogan, with one user quipping, 'When it rains, it really does pour.' Morton Salt, which employs nearly 3,000 people across the U.S., Canada, and the Bahamas, produces table salt, water softeners, and ice-melting products. In a brief statement, the company confirmed the wall collapse at its storage facility but offered no further details on the cause.

article_content: In response to a sharp rise in thefts, Iceland supermarkets across the UK have begun locking up popular meat products like lamb in secure, alarm-equipped boxes — similar to those used for electronics. The move, rolled out in hundreds of stores, aims to deter shoplifters who’ve been slipping meat into their clothing and fleeing the store, leaving the goods unusable. While Iceland claims the boxes help keep products available for paying customers, many shoppers say they’re heartbroken to see food treated like contraband. Simon Wightman, a father of three from Kent, described finding his weekly lamb in a security box as deeply saddening: 'People aren’t stealing for fun — they’re stealing because they’re hungry.' Food charities echo this sentiment, noting that food bank demand has surged by over 30% in some areas since the 2009 recession, with more than 200,000 Britons now relying on emergency food aid. Iceland tested similar security measures for cheese and bacon, but found them less effective; lamb remains the primary target due to its popularity and price. Spokesperson Amy Globe stressed the boxes are not punishment, but a practical step to reduce losses and maintain supply. Meanwhile, Trussell Trust’s Molly Hodson warned that parents are skipping meals to feed their children — and when that’s not enough, some feel they have no choice but to steal. The real issue, critics argue, isn’t shoplifting — it’s a system where basic nutrition is out of reach for too many.

article_content: A triplex penthouse under construction atop 50 UN Plaza in Manhattan will cost prospective buyers $100 million, its developers have announced. When completed in December 2014, the residence will feature 14 bedrooms, 13 full bathrooms, a fireplace, and 1,500 square feet of outdoor space—including an infinity-edge pool. Designed by renowned architect Norman Foster, the 88-story building is located directly across from the United Nations headquarters and will offer sweeping views of the East River and the Chrysler Building. The developers purchased the site in 2007 for $160 million, but construction was delayed for several years due to the economic recession. Condominium prices in the building will start at $2.8 million for a one-bedroom unit, with two-bedroom units priced between $3.6 million and $9.4 million, according to Bloomberg News. Originally planned as a duplex, the penthouse was redesigned as a triplex in response to strong demand for ultra-luxury residences in New York City, Zeckendorf Development representatives told the Financial Times. They noted that final pricing may still change. The project, a collaboration between Zeckendorf Development and Eyal Ofer’s Global Holdings, marks Foster + Partners’ first residential development in the United States. Developers aim to attract wealthy international clients, including diplomats, citing the building’s global design and prime location. 'Everything about this building is international—from its location and design to the people we are looking to attract,' said William Zeckendorf in the Financial Times. 'We want to draw the wealthiest individuals seeking exceptional architecture and amenities, whether from abroad or within the domestic market.' While this penthouse ranks among New York’s most expensive properties, it is not the most costly. Earlier in 2013, the Pierre Hotel penthouse on the Upper East Side was listed for $125 million. Hedge fund manager Steven Cohen’s downtown penthouse was marketed for $115 million, and former Citigroup chairman Sandy Weill sold his 15 Central Park West apartment for $88 million in February 2012. Two penthouses at One57 are expected to sell for $90 million each.

article_content: Germany’s dominance in the Tour de France sprints continued on Thursday as Andre Greipel claimed victory in Reims during the 194-kilometre sixth stage from Arras. Rain-slicked roads triggered multiple crashes, forcing several riders to abandon the race. Greipel, riding for Lotto-Belisol, capitalized on the absence of Marcel Kittel — the previous sprint king and winner of Stages 1, 3, and 4 — who withdrew due to a mechanical issue. This allowed Greipel, who had struggled for positioning in earlier sprints, to surge ahead in the final meters, crossing the line with arms raised in triumph. His win marked his sixth career Tour de France stage victory. Alexander Kristoff (Katusha) finished second, with Samuel Dumoulin (Ag2r La Mondiale) in third. Vincenzo Nibali (Astana) remained safely in the peloton to retain the yellow jersey he won on Stage 2 in Sheffield. Team Sky endured another tough day: Spaniard Xabier Zandio joined Chris Froome in withdrawing after a crash, leaving Richie Porte with only six teammates remaining less than a week into the race. Other notable abandonments included Egor Silin (Katusha), Arnaud Demare (FDJ), and Jesus Hernandez (Tinkoff-Saxo). Despite fears of crosswinds splitting the peloton, the field stayed tightly knit throughout the stage. A four-rider breakaway led by Jerome Pineau, Thomas Leezer, Luis Mate, and Arnaud Gerard held a 1:30 advantage with 65km to go, but was reeled in before the final climb. In the final kilometers, nine roundabouts and drying asphalt created chaotic conditions. Omega Pharma-QuickStep led the charge for Mark Renshaw, while Cannondale, Europcar, and Katusha also played key roles. Michal Kwiatkowski launched a late attack at the flamme rouge but was caught with 300m to go. Greipel then exploded past Renshaw to claim the win. Greipel told British Eurosport: 'It was a nervous day. I stayed in front the whole time. With so many roundabouts, there was no perfect leadout. But I had a good wheel beside me. At 250 metres, I just went all-in.' Richie Porte added: 'It was a stressful day. Horrible, honestly. We lost Xabi, but the rest of us stayed out of trouble. Now we fight on.' Nibali’s lead remains intact heading into Friday’s 234.5km Stage 7 from Epernay to Nancy — another stage expected to end in a mass sprint.

article_content: In June 2013, former President Barack Obama and his family traveled to Ireland for a brief but costly official visit tied to the G-8 summit in Belfast. While the president attended high-level international meetings, First Lady Michelle Obama and their two daughters spent several days in Dublin, where their stay—including luxury hotel accommodations, meals, and transportation—cost taxpayers more than $250,000. The family stayed in the Princess Grace Suite at Dublin’s prestigious Shelbourne Hotel, a spacious two-bedroom residence priced at $3,300 per night, complete with butler service and private dining. Additional lodging was arranged at the Westbury Hotel for members of the First Lady’s security and support team. The total cost of the trip reached approximately $7.7 million, primarily due to Air Force One’s operational expenses. The presidential jet flew for over 33 hours at a rate of nearly $230,000 per hour, accounting for nearly all of the spending. Although the White House classified the Dublin portion as an official engagement—citing visits to Trinity College, the Book of Kells, and a Riverdance performance—the itinerary closely mirrored that of a leisurely cultural tour. Michelle Obama even remarked to children that the college library felt 'like Hogwarts,' drawing both admiration and playful critique. Over $114,000 was spent on rental vehicles, mostly to transport Secret Service agents, while security personnel occupied multiple hotels across Dublin. These expenses were disclosed only after Judicial Watch, a government watchdog group, successfully sued for records under the Freedom of Information Act. Tom Fitton, the group’s president, condemned the trip as an inappropriate use of public funds, calling it a 'luxury vacation' disguised as diplomacy. Critics noted that the 2011 Obama trip to Ireland had already cost $2.6 million, making the 2013 expenditure unusually high—even for a presidential delegation requiring extensive protection. Despite the controversy, such travel is standard protocol for U.S. presidents and their families abroad. Security, logistics, and diplomatic protocol necessitate large support teams, and accommodations are typically chosen based on safety and accessibility—not luxury. Still, the optics of lavish spending during economic hardship have fueled public debate about transparency and accountability in government expenditures.

Iindlela zonke zokuhamba ziyafika kwiR7.7m, ngokukhawuleza ukuba uAir Force One uyayihamba ngalinye amaphuzu 230,000, kwaye kuyafika kwiR7,670,476.80. article_content: On Wednesday, Lok Sabha opposition leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury marked the seventh anniversary of the 2016 demonetization with a pointed critique of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Posting on X (formerly Twitter), Chowdhury challenged the PM: 'Respected PM @narendramodi Ji, today marks the 7th anniversary of #DEMONITIZATION — hailed as your visionary step to eradicate black money from India. Should we celebrate this milestone, or mourn what many see as an abysmal failure?' On November 8, 2016, the Indian government withdrew the legal tender status of ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes, citing goals such as curbing black money, eliminating counterfeit currency, disrupting terror financing, formalizing the economy, expanding the tax base, and accelerating digital payments. The government has repeatedly cited a significant rise in Income Tax Returns (ITRs) filed since the move as evidence of improved tax compliance and formalization. Prime Minister Modi has stated that demonetization contributed to greater transparency and national progress. However, critics contend that much of the so-called black money was shifted overseas rather than eradicated. Political parties continue to promise recovery of these funds and prosecution of those involved. In unrelated economic news, India’s FMCG sector saw a 9% value and 8.6% volume growth in the September quarter of 2023, driven by stronger rural demand. Meanwhile, Snapchat’s user base in India doubled to 200 million in a year, fueled by its Spotlight feature. The finance ministry is also considering slowing capital expenditure hikes in the FY25 interim budget to meet fiscal consolidation targets.

Uwayeza kwiX (eziyisizwe se-Twitter): 'Umlando wami uPM @narendramodi Ji, ukuqala kwesikhathi esibini saseNkombo yezikhathi ezintathu zeminyaka engu-7 kwe-Demonetization, eyenzekileyo njengomthombo wakho othembekileyo ukuthatha imali yesifiso kwiIndia. Kuyenza ntoni ukuzivikela esikhathini esibini, noma ukuthula ngokushesha ukuthi kufuneka ukubhala?' Kwesikhathi ka-November 8, 2016, izwe elihlukele iinkonzo zikaR500 neR1000 ezinokuthi ziyinhlanzeko, ezinokuthi zinokuthola imali yesifiso, ukukhuphuka kwezikhathi ezifanayo, ukugcina ukuthi izindlela zokuthenga zokuthiwa, ukuba iziqhinga ezifanayo, ukubuyisela izixhobo zokuthenga, nokulungisa iintlanga zokuthenga. Izwe elihlukele lizikhetha ukubuyeza kwezinkonzo zokuthenga zeminyaka engu-7 ezingaphansi kwezikhathi ezintathu, ukuthi kuyinto enokuthi kungenzeka ukuthi kufuneka ukuthola imali yesifiso, nokulungisa izixhobo zokuthenga. UPM Modi wayebhekisa ukuthi ukuqhubeka kwesikhathi esibini saseNkombo yezikhathi ezintathu kuyinto enokuthi kungenzeka ukuthi kufuneka ukuthola imali yesifiso, nokulungisa izixhobo zokuthenga. Kodwa, abaninzi bathi ukuthi imali yesifiso emnyakeni engu-7 ayikho, kodwa yayiphiwa ekhaya. Abaphenduli abaninzi bakhuluma ngokuthi babuyise imali, nokuthi bawubhekisa ngezithelo ezinokuthi ziyinhlanzeko. Ngesikhathi esibini, iziqhinga ze-FMCG eIndia zazibuyeza ngokuthi 9% ngokucacisa, 8.6% ngokuphumelela, ngokuphakamisa kwezinyathelo ezinene kwiindawo ezinene. Izwe elihlukele lizikhetha ukuba ukubuyisela kwezixhobo zokuthenga ezinokuthi ziyinhlanzeko kwindaba yefika ye-FY25 ukuthi bazobuyisela izixhobo zokuthenga.

article_content: A group of prominent British musicians has appealed to Russian President Vladimir Putin to ensure a fair hearing for three members of the punk band Pussy Riot, who are facing up to seven years in prison for a protest performance inside Moscow’s Church of Christ the Saviour. In a letter to The Times, artists including Jarvis Cocker, Pete Townshend, Martha Wainwright, and Neil Tennant described the act as a 'minor breach of the peace' and condemned the severity of the punishment as 'entirely disproportionate'. The women — Nadezhda Tolokonnikova (22), Yekaterina Samutsevich (29), and Maria Alyokhina (24) — staged what they called a 'punk prayer' in February, singing an anti-Putin message in a restricted area of the cathedral reserved for clergy. They were arrested in March and charged with hooliganism motivated by religious hatred. Though they acknowledged possibly offending worshippers, they maintain their actions were politically motivated and not criminally malicious. The musicians expressed deep concern over reports that the women have allegedly been denied adequate food and forced to appear in court inside a glass cage. Their appeal coincides with Putin’s current visit to the UK, where they are urging him to recognize artistic dissent as a fundamental democratic right. Support for Pussy Riot has grown internationally, with figures such as Sting and the Red Hot Chili Peppers joining the call for justice. Ten other participants and journalists were present during the protest but were not arrested. The three defendants say they sought to spark change in Russia — even if their method was ethically questionable — but insist they are innocent of the charges.

article_content: A new report warns that blood transfusions may be responsible for the silent spread of variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (vCJD) in the UK population. Up to 30,000 Britons may be carrying infectious prions—abnormal proteins that cause fatal brain damage—in a dormant state, double the previous estimate. The human form of mad cow disease, vCJD, leads to rapid neurological decline and is almost always fatal within a year of symptom onset. Although dietary exposure to infected beef was largely eliminated after the 1989 outbreak, which prompted the culling of millions of cattle, prions persist in the blood supply. Scientists believe the current death toll of 176 could rise more than fivefold, as infected blood donations continue to pose a risk. Former Health Secretary Frank Dobson has urged the government to launch a nationwide screening program for blood donors, saying 'everything humanly possible should be done to develop a blood test.' He added, 'There is no room for complacency.' A positive test could lead to population-wide screening if prevalence exceeds expectations. The Department of Health maintains that the UK has one of the safest blood supplies in the world and continues to encourage donations from all age groups. No new clinical cases of vCJD have been reported in two years, and there is no evidence linking any transfusion after 1999 to a vCJD case. To reduce future risk, experts suggest recruiting young donors born after 1996, who would not have consumed infected beef during the peak exposure period.

IvCJD, umthetho wezinye izinto eziyindoda, uzokukhanya kakhulu kanye nokuphatha kwezinhlelo zomthetho kanti izokufa kakhulu ngonyaka wokungena kwezinto.
